rows.key_quote: JOYY reported Q2 2026 revenue of $591M, up 16.3% YoY and 6.3% QoQ, with non-GAAP operating profit of $49M, up 28.2% YoY. Social entertainment revenue grew 7.4% YoY, BIGO Ads grew 53.1% YoY, and SHOPLINE grew 28.6% YoY. Management raised full-year non-GAAP operating income growth guidance to around 20% (from teens), driven by better-than-expected H1 performance. Q3 revenue guidance of $602-622M implies 11.4%-15.2% YoY growth.

Q2 2026 net revenue was RMB 3.57 billion, down from RMB 3.91 billion in Q1 and RMB 5.22 billion a year ago, with non-GAAP net profit of RMB 455 million versus RMB 946 million in Q1 and RMB 1.85 billion a year ago. The company guided Q3 non-GAAP net income between RMB 400-500 million, implying a 67-73% YoY decline. Management cited a late-June industry liquidity crisis and a nationwide collections crackdown, causing a sharp reversal in risk metrics in August with C-M2 expected to rise ~25% sequentially. They plan to maintain strict risk controls, expecting volume not to return to Q2 levels for two to three quarters.

Q2 FY2026 net revenue was RMB 620 million, down 1.5% YoY, but operating income rose 34% YoY to RMB 216 million with an operating margin of 34.8%. Non-GAAP net income was RMB 238 million, up 25.9% YoY and 77.8% QoQ. First-half performance-based income surged 364% YoY to RMB 238 million, while US-dollar AUM grew 11.7% YoY to $6.5 billion despite overseas RM headcount declining 36.2%. Management maintained full-year operating margin guidance above 30% and emphasized the Singapore AI Wealth Management Department proof point (AUM from <$100M to >$400M, monthly profitability in July 2026) as evidence of a scalable model.

Zoom reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.28 billion, up 4.9% YoY, $7 million above the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.55, $0.08 above the high end of guidance, and non-GAAP operating margin was 40%. Enterprise revenue grew 7.8% YoY, the strongest in three years, while RPO grew 14% YoY. Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, now expecting $5.085-$5.095 billion (4.5% YoY growth at midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS of $6.08-$6.12, while also raising free cash flow outlook to $1.78-$1.82 billion.

Fiscal 2026 revenue grew 14% with full-year GAAP and non-GAAP EPS up 20% each, but Q4 non-GAAP EPS beat at $4.03 (up 47%) while GAAP EPS fell slightly to $1.34. Management reset FY2027 guidance lower, expecting total revenue growth of 9%-10% (vs 14% in FY2026) due to deliberate actions in DIY tax, desktop declines, and Mailchimp stagnation. Online paying customers growth slowed to 3%, and management acknowledged losing quality DIY tax customers to low-cost providers, with a plan to rebuild the funnel at lower ARPC. The company also accelerated buybacks in Q4 and announced FY2027 non-GAAP EPS growth of 23%-24% including share-based compensation.

Q4 FY2026 reported net sales declined 2.2% to $465M, but adjusted net sales rose 0.4% excluding discontinued TSA sales. Adjusted operating income grew 17.5%, and adjusted EPS rose to $1.46 from $1.34. Full-year results hit records for net sales, gross profit, and operating income. For FY2027, management guides to mid-single-digit revenue growth, 100 bps gross margin expansion, and a Q1 operating income decline of ~15% due to a 250 bps Cyclospora sales headwind.

Kanzhun reported Q2 2026 revenue of RMB 2.4 billion, up 14% YoY, with adjusted operating margin expanding to 43.8% (up 1.9pp YoY). MAU hit a record 70 million, and paid enterprise customers rose 11% to 7.2 million. Management guided Q3 revenue of RMB 2.41-2.5 billion, implying 11.4%-15.6% YoY growth, and increased shareholder returns to over $530 million for 2026, exceeding 100% of prior-year adjusted net income.

Box reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $321M, up 9% YoY (11% cc), exceeding guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.40 above the $0.39 guide. Net retention rate was 106%, above guidance and up from 103% a year ago; billings grew 17% YoY to $310M and RPO reached $1.7B, up 15%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by $10M to ~$1.29B (10% YoY growth) and EPS to ~$1.54, citing strong Enterprise Advanced adoption and AI momentum. Operating margin expanded 90 bps to 29.4%, with FX headwinds partially offsetting robust demand.

Citi Trends reported Q2 FY2026 (note the transcript says FY2026, not FY2027) total sales of $211.6 million, a 10.9% increase, with comparable sales up 10.5% (19.7% on a two-year basis). Adjusted EBITDA was $5.5 million, a $6.6 million improvement over last year's loss. The company raised its full-year comparable sales growth guidance to 9%-11% (from 8%-10%) and adjusted EBITDA to $38-$42 million (from $35-$40 million). Management noted continued momentum into Q3 with a ~25% two-year comp stack during back-to-school.

Tuya reported Q2 2026 revenue of $92.9M, up 16% YoY, accelerating from 8.3% in Q1. PaaS revenue grew 16.9% to $67.9M, while AI application and other segments grew only 3.9% to $11.5M. Blended gross margin was 46.3%, with PaaS margin at 46.8%, down YoY due to semiconductor cost increases. Non-GAAP operating margin held at 10.3%, and net cash from operations was $6.2M. Management expects gradual demand recovery with continued growth, but did not provide specific guidance.

DICK'S Sporting Goods reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net sales of $5.59 billion, up 53.2%, driven by the Foot Locker acquisition and a 4.9% comp at DICK'S. The company lowered full-year EPS guidance to $11-$12 from $13.50-$14.50, citing promotional pressure and Foot Locker weakness. DICK'S comp expectations were maintained at 2.5%-4%, but operating margin guidance was cut. Foot Locker comp guidance was reduced to -2% to flat, and its operating loss is now expected.

nCino reported Q2 FY2027 total revenues of $161M (+8% YoY) and subscription revenues of $143.5M (+10% YoY, +10% cc), beating guidance by approximately $1.3M. Non-U.S. subscription revenues grew 13% YoY to $30.9M, while U.S. mortgage subscription revenues declined 1% to $20.6M. Non-GAAP operating income was $40.8M (25% margin), up 36% YoY, and free cash flow was $34M, up 170%. The company raised full-year revenue and operating income guidance, with subscription revenue guidance raised to $573.5M-$576.5M and non-GAAP operating income to $171M-$174M, but lowered U.S. mortgage outlook due to higher IMB churn.

Electromed reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $19.4 million, up 11.6% YoY, with operating income of $3.8 million, up 26% YoY, and diluted EPS of $0.39, a quarterly record. Full-year revenue grew 15.3% to $73.8 million, with operating margin expanding from 15.1% to 18.8%. Management guided to another year of double-digit top-line growth, operating leverage, and strong cash flow for FY2027, while raising the fiscal 2027 revenue-per-rep target range to $1.05M-$1.15M. CEO Jim Cunniff announced his retirement effective April 2027, with a succession planning process underway.

Semtech reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $342 million, up 33% YoY and 17% sequentially, beating the high end of guidance. Adjusted EPS was $0.71, up 73% YoY, exceeding guidance. Data center revenue hit a record $100 million, up 91% YoY, with strong 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge ramp. Guidance for Q3 projects revenue of $410 million (+54% YoY) and EPS of $1.05 (+119% YoY), with data center revenue up 160% YoY. The company announced the divestiture of its cellular module business, expecting an EPS-neutral deal and structural gross margin improvement.

Q2 FY2026 revenue more than doubled to EUR 282.8 million (up 432% YoY), EBITDA rose 106% to EUR 160.6 million, and net profit grew 73% to EUR 95 million. Adjusted fleet utilization reached 91% for the quarter. Backlog stood at EUR 2.5 billion, up 23% YoY, with 77% at FID. Management guided revenue to EUR 854-944 million and EBITDA of EUR 420-510 million for FY2026, unchanged from prior guidance, and reported strong commercial momentum and several preferred supplier agreements.

Woodside reported H1 FY2026 production of 86.5 MMboe, free cash flow up over 150% YoY to $352 million, EBITDA of $4.6 billion, and underlying NPAT of $1.3 billion. The board declared a fully franked interim dividend of $0.57 per share. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance for Scarborough first LNG in Q4 and announced a structural cost-out target of $350 million per year from 2028, while retiring Scope 3 targets and initiating a strategic review of Beaumont New Ammonia. Gearing of 20.6% is temporarily above the 10-20% target but expected to fall below 20% by year-end.

Scotiabank reported record EPS of CAD 2.28, up 21% YoY, with ROE of 14.2%, exceeding its medium-term target ahead of schedule. Revenue grew 16% YoY with operating leverage positive for the tenth consecutive quarter and CET1 ratio at 13.1%. Canadian Banking ROE improved 160 bps sequentially to 19.4%, and GBM delivered record net income. Guidance remains positive with expectations to finish the year strong, though Q4 includes a 15 bps CET1 impact from AIRB migration.

BMO Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS was CAD 3.96, up 22% YoY, on record net income of CAD 2.9 billion. Revenue grew 11% YoY with positive operating leverage of 1.6%; ROE improved to 14% (up 200 bps YoY). Management reaffirmed the 15% ROE target exiting fiscal 2027 and expects Q4 impaired PCL to be in line with Q3, maintaining 2026 guidance. The bank announced a new NCIB for up to 25 million shares and expects divestitures to add 50 bps to CET1.

Q2 FY2026 total net revenues fell 4.3% YoY to RMB 24.7 billion, at the low end of guidance, as consumers remained highly selective. Non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders was RMB 392.2 million (down from RMB 2.1 billion), dragged by a one-time withholding tax adjustment; adjusted for that, underlying non-GAAP net profit was RMB 2.0 billion with a 7.9% net margin. Gross margin slipped 20 bps to 23.3%, and non-GAAP operating margin declined to 8.1% from 9.3%. For Q3, management guided revenue down 5% to 0% YoY and expects full-year revenue slightly negative, citing persistent macro softness.

Tuniu reported Q2 2026 net revenues of CNY 138.9 million, up 3% YoY, with packaged tours up 7% to CNY 121.1 million and other revenues down 17% to CNY 17.8 million. GAAP net income was CNY 0.7 million and non-GAAP net income was CNY 2.2 million, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of non-GAAP profitability. Gross profit fell 11% YoY to CNY 76.4 million, while operating expenses rose 5% to CNY 82.5 million. For Q3 2026, the company guides net revenues of CNY 202.1-212.2 million, implying 0% to 5% YoY growth, reflecting persistent outbound travel headwinds.

Schmid's H1 2026 revenue rose to EUR 46.0 million from a weak prior-year half, with equipment revenues jumping to EUR 39.4 million from EUR 10.7 million. Order intake accelerated sharply to EUR 96.6 million year-to-date, including EUR 52.3 million in the last eight weeks, leading management to raise full-year order intake guidance to EUR 125-150 million and expect the upper half. However, adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 6-9% from prior >12%, reflecting lower scale and margin mix; revenue guidance of at least EUR 100 million was maintained. The balance sheet was repaired via a EUR 30.75 million debt-to-equity swap and EUR 33 million raised, with total debt reduced from EUR 53 million to about EUR 23 million.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $6.7M, up 118% YoY from $3.1M, with gross margin expanding to 66.6% from 55.1%. GPU fleet grew 224% to 3,088, and the company signed 21 new contracts totaling $169.7M, bringing total signed contract value to $282.5M. Operating loss widened to $7.7M from $2.2M YoY due to higher D&A, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sequentially to $0.8M. Management did not reaffirm the $300M ARR target but noted they are not demand constrained, with land/power being the primary gating factor.

Gold Fields reported a strong H1 FY2026 with attributable production up 12% to 1.267 million ounces and sales volumes up 18%, driven by a 51% higher average realized gold price of $4,678/oz. Adjusted free cash flow more than doubled to $2.225 billion (11% yield), and headline earnings per share more than doubled. All-in sustaining costs rose 13% to $1,893/oz due to royalties, currency, and inflation, but guidance is unchanged with production tracking to the upper end and costs to the mid/lower end of ranges. Shareholder returns were bolstered with an interim dividend up 132% and an additional $500 million allocated to buybacks, while net debt to EBITDA fell to 0.06x.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was RMB 77.9 million, down 31% YoY from RMB 113.3 million but up 203% sequentially from RMB 25.7 million. Gross margin was 61.2%, stable. Adjusted operating loss was RMB 62 million and adjusted net loss was RMB 58.5 million. The company withdrew its FY2026 revenue guidance of RMB 600 million due to regulatory uncertainty after a June light sport aircraft accident, with no replacement guidance provided.

PicPay reported a strong Q2 2026, with managerial revenues of BRL 3.7 billion (up 59% YoY, 17% QoQ), adjusted net income of BRL 283 million (up 135% YoY, up 67% QoQ), and adjusted ROE of 20.2%. Management beat guidance on credit portfolio, revenues, NII, gross profit, and net income, with credit portfolio at BRL 31.9 billion (3% above guidance) and gross profit 8.4% above guidance. Guidance for Q3 2026 expects continued growth with managerial revenues around BRL 4 billion, but adjusted net income is expected to decline sequentially to ~BRL 265 million due to the normalization of the Lei do Bem tax benefit and higher cost of risk. The company closed the Kovr acquisition (now KEV Seguros) in August 2026, expecting BRL 80-100 million net income contribution for August-December 2026.

NAPCO Security Technologies reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $55.8 million, up 10% YoY, with recurring service revenue up 12.9% to $25.3 million and equipment revenue up 7.7% to $30.5 million. GAAP net income rose 52.7% to $17.8 million ($0.50 per diluted share), and adjusted EBITDA increased 44.3% to $20.6 million. Full-year revenue reached a record $202.3 million, with non-GAAP EPS up 34.5% to $1.60. Management highlighted 40% YoY growth in radio unit sales and a rising recurring revenue run rate, while noting supply chain challenges and tariff-related costs as headwinds. The company raised its quarterly dividend by 13.3% to $0.17 per share.

Q2 2026 revenue was RMB 19.74 billion, up 8% YoY and 51.5% QoQ; vehicle deliveries reached 103,295 units, up 65% QoQ. Gross margin was 20.7%, above 20% for the second consecutive quarter, though vehicle margin fell YoY to 12.1% due to production generation transition. Net loss narrowed to RMB 1.34 billion from RMB 1.7 billion QoQ. Q3 2026 guidance calls for deliveries of 115,000-121,000 units and revenue of RMB 21.7-23.4 billion, implying QoQ growth of 9.9%-18.5%. XPeng Robotics raised over $900 million at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, led by IDG, with plans to start scaled production of its IRON humanoid robot by year-end.

In Q2 2026, X Financial reported net revenue of RMB 993.6 million, down 56.3% YoY and 15.5% sequentially, with net income of RMB 47 million, up 23.8% sequentially. Loan origination fell 70.2% YoY to RMB 11.63 billion, and the outstanding loan balance declined 61.5% YoY to RMB 24.97 billion. Both delinquency rates improved sequentially for the first time in several quarters, but management did not provide quantitative guidance for Q3 due to material uncertainties, while maintaining a conservative stance on credit and capital preservation.

PDD reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 112.4 billion, up 8% YoY, while net income declined 12% to RMB 27.2 billion. GAAP operating profit rose 8% to RMB 27.8 billion, but non-GAAP operating margin contracted to 26% from 27%. Management noted slower-than-expected first-party brand rollout and significant near-term impact from EU customs duty changes on cross-border orders.

The9 reported Q2 2026 net income of $32 million, up 39% quarter-over-quarter, driven by fair value recognition of 9BIT tokens, with half-year net income of $55 million. The9bit reached 8 million registered users and 110,000 user-created games, but revenue from the platform remains small, with management expecting stronger revenue growth in the second half after in-game purchase support launches. The pending NYB SPAC combination with RFAI, which would give The9 a 15%-16% stake in a combined company valued around $7.7 billion, was approved by RFAI shareholders, though the listing timeline remains uncertain. Management outlined a strategic repositioning around The9bit, but the platform's current revenue scale and reliance on token-based valuation raise concerns about sustainability and execution.

Q2 FY2026 revenue reached $50.1 million, up 138% YoY and 78% QoQ, beating raised guidance of $44 million by $6.1 million. H1 revenue was $78.4 million, up 99% YoY. Operating loss narrowed to $2.2 million in Q2 from $41.1 million in Q1, due largely to reduced share-based compensation. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to at least $200 million from $137-$200 million, and targets $450-$500 million for 2027. Cash stood at $179.4 million at end of H1, boosted by convertible debt and financing activities.

Intchains reported first-half FY2026 revenue of RMB 11.1 million and a net loss per share of RMB 1.22 against the backdrop of cyclical softness in outgoing demand and PRC mining machine sales restrictions. Management provided no specific financial guidance for H2, noting continued market headwinds but expressing confidence that their new ASIC tape-out completed in July will enable commercial launch in Q4 2026 with meaningful impact expected in fiscal 2027. The company also announced a $15 million share repurchase program funded by existing cash balances.

ZKH reported Q2 FY26 GMV growth of 18.9% YoY and net revenue growth of 12.8%, marking the fastest pace in recent quarters. The company achieved a significant financial milestone by turning to positive operating profit for the first time, with non-GAAP adjusted net income reaching RMB 39 million compared to a loss last year. Management raised guidance expectations for H2 GMV acceleration and reiterated confidence in achieving full-year growth targets of 15%-20%.

Largo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $44 million (up 68.5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA returning to positive at $2.7 million after a loss in the prior year period, driven by higher vanadium volumes (+53%) and improved pricing ($6.96/lb). Management maintained full-year guidance for vanadium production but introduced initial volume guidance for new copper-PGM concentrate (300-380 tons/month) following the start of commercial-scale output in August. Significant non-cash items, including a write-down on vanadium assets and deferred tax expenses, contributed to a reported net loss of $22.7 million despite operational improvements.

BJ's Wholesale Club reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $6.1 billion (up 15.9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.36 (up 19%), both beating expectations driven by strong gas business performance and membership growth to a new milestone of 8.5 million members. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60-$4.80 while maintaining comparable club sales growth guidance at 2%-3%. The quarter highlighted durable momentum with traffic accelerating for the 18th consecutive quarter, though merchandise gross margin contracted approximately 20 basis points due to continued price investments.

Buckle reported Q2 FY27 net sales of $319.8 million (up 4.6% YoY) and diluted EPS of $0.87, missing the prior year's $0.89 per share despite a comparable store sales increase of 2.1%. Gross margin expanded to 47.8%, driven by tariff refunds and private label mix shifts which offset higher SG&A expenses including marketing increases. Management reiterated its policy against providing future guidance.

Prospect Capital reported Q4 FY26 Net Investment Income of $78 million ($0.15/share) and NAV of $2.9 billion, which were in-line with the prior quarter but missed implied expectations given a significant one-time exit gain from Valley Electric Company that was not included in recurring NII guidance comparisons. Management highlighted strong balance sheet metrics including 66% unencumbered assets and reduced nonaccruals at 0.7%, while noting that interest income is now predominantly cash-based (91%) following a reduction in payment-in-kind income to 10%. The company announced monthly distributions of $0.035 per share for September and October, maintaining its long history of shareholder returns.

In Q2 FY2026, total revenue declined 5.7% year-over-year to RMB 34.1 billion (implied from segment sum), while Non-GAAP net income surged 74.9% YoY to RMB 3.185 billion driven by gross margin expansion and lower operating expenses. Existing home transaction services returned to growth with GTV up 6.3%, whereas new home, renovation, and rental segments faced revenue pressure or declines due to market adjustments and strategic channel exits. Management emphasized strict financial discipline, a leaner cost structure, and resource reallocation toward high-quality projects rather than broad expansion.

Futu reported Q2 FY26 revenue of HKD 7.2 billion (up 36% YoY) and net income of HKD 3.6 billion (up 42% YoY), beating market consensus on a record trading volume backdrop. Management raised blended CAC guidance for the full year to HKD 2,500-HKD 3,000 while noting that Q3 run-rate metrics are trending modestly softer due to cooling retail sentiment and regulatory outflows in Mainland China.

FlashEx reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of CNY 940.3 million, a year-over-year decrease driven by intensifying marketing competition and industry anti-involution trends. Gross margin contracted to 10.2% from the prior year's 12%, while non-GAAP income from operations fell significantly due to losses on fair value changes in long-term investments.

Flowers Foods reported a miss on Q2 FY26 results with net sales declining 4% YoY to $5.07B-$5.14B (full-year guidance revised down) and adjusted EBITDA falling 19%. Gross margin contracted by 40 bps due to lower volumes, while the company updated its full-year outlook for EPS ($0.75-$0.85), sales, and EBITDA downward.

Huize reported strong first-half FY26 results with GWP reaching a record RMB 4.2 billion (up ~30% YoY) and FYP surging to RMB 2.76 billion (up ~49% YoY). Net profit attributable to common shareholders increased to RMB 25.3 million, supported by improved operating efficiency with total expenses dropping to RMB 175 million. Management expressed confidence in its AI-native strategy and international expansion while noting continued investment in AI infrastructure.

Walmart reported Q2 FY2027 enterprise net sales growth of 5% in constant currency and adjusted operating income growth of 17.4%, driven by e-commerce (up 23%) and strong performance from Marketplace, advertising, and membership businesses. Management raised full-year guidance for both sales (to 4%-5%) and operating income (to 7%-8.5%), citing confidence in the omni-channel model despite a specific headwind of approximately 125 basis points to U.S. comp sales from Maximum Fair Price drug regulations.

Aurora Mobile reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 101.2 million (up 13% YoY), driven by a record Developer Subscription Services quarter of RMB 70.7 million and global flagship EngageLab ARR reaching $14.6 million (+170% YoY). The company achieved its fifth consecutive quarter of GAAP net profit with gross margin expanding 197 bps to approximately 58%, while generating positive operating cash flow of RMB 23.3 million and repurchasing 44,000 ADS.

Total revenues of $706 million slightly beat the midpoint of guidance while gross margin expanded to 14.6%, also above the midpoint range. Adjusted pre-tax income missed expectations at a loss of $2 million due to lower-than-expected joint venture income, marking the first time in 23 quarters that adjusted pre-tax finished below guidance. Management provided Q4 revenue guidance between $800M-$900M and expects gross margins to improve further to a range of 15%-16.5%.

Fiscal Q4 FY26 net sales increased 4.2% to $280.4 million driven by a 1.4% volume gain and 2.8% price increase, though gross profit declined 9.5% due to recall costs ($2.7M), higher freight, and manufacturing inefficiencies resulting in a margin contraction from 18.1% to 15.7%. Diluted EPS fell to $0.71 per share compared to $1.15 last year as the company navigates input cost volatility and customer-related charges.

In the first half of FY2026, total revenue reached RMB 124 million, representing a 33.7% year-over-year increase driven by surging demand in AI advertising and institutional services. Gross profit margin expanded significantly to 66.4%, up from 54.4% the prior period, while net income turned positive at RMB 15.4 million compared to a loss of RMB 4.8 million last year. Management highlighted strong growth engines in AI content coverage and industrial services without providing specific forward guidance figures.

NovaBridge Biosciences reported a debt-free balance sheet with approximately $216 million in cash and investments as of June 30, 2026, supporting operations through anticipated phase III interim data readouts for givastomig in 2028. The company highlighted significant regulatory progress for its lead oncology program givastomig, including FDA Fast Track designation and potential eligibility for an Accelerated Approval Pathway in first-line HER2 negative gastroesophageal cancer following a Type B meeting. Management outlined plans to initiate phase III studies as early as the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to planning activities.

Nordson reported record Q3 FY26 sales of $818 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $3.25 (up 19%), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of $3,000-$3,750M and adjusted earnings to $11.80-$12.00 per share, citing sustained order momentum and backlog growth up 35% YoY.

Advance Auto Parts reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $2 billion with a slight decline in comparable sales driven by low double-digit DIY weakness and weather headwinds that offset Pro channel growth. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for same-SKU inflation at approximately 3% and adjusted operating income margins between 3.8%-4.5%, while raising diluted EPS guidance to $2.60-$3.30 due to higher interest income from a strong cash balance of $3.1 billion.

Navios Maritime Partners reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $410 million (up 25% YoY) and net income of $167.9 million on a fleet with lower available days but significantly higher TCE rates across all segments. Management raised the common unit repurchase authorization to $200 million, doubling the prior program size while maintaining liquidity for newbuilding deliveries. The company continues to de-lever its balance sheet toward a 20%-25% net LTV target amidst strong contracted revenue visibility extending through 2037.

NetEase reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of RMB 30.1 billion ($4.4B), representing a 10% year-over-year increase but a slight quarter-over-quarter decline in online games net revenue (-2%). Gross profit margin expanded to 70.5%, driven by lower platform sharing costs and improved margins across segments, while non-GAAP EPS was $1.78 per ADS ($0.36/share). Management highlighted strong performance from titles like 'Sea of Remnants' post-optimization and global hits like 'Marvel Rivals', but noted a leaner new game pipeline ahead.

Total revenue for Q2 FY2026 was $1.5 million, representing a significant decrease of 52% year-over-year and approximately 20% sequentially from the first quarter. The company reported a net loss of $4.6 million compared to a prior period loss of $534k in Q2 last year, driven by lower portfolio cash generation and higher interest expenses on convertible notes before their subsequent extinguishment.

Total net revenues exceeded the high end of guidance at CNY 6.61 billion (up 32.4% YoY), while non-GAAP operating profit surged to CNY 210 million (up 70.1%). The company raised its Q3 revenue guidance range to CNY 6.34-6.44 billion, anticipating growth of 23.1%-25.1%. Management highlighted strong demand for pre-owned devices driven by new device price hikes and robust trade-in programs.

Q2 FY2026 reported revenue increased 55% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA rose 74%, driven by a broad-based production recovery across all assets including Bolivar (+17%) and San Lucas. However, the quarter was significantly impacted by non-operating items: a $15.8 million non-cash fair value loss on Glencore CVRs due to rising zinc price expectations and an unusually high income tax expense of $36.1 million triggered by Bolivia's exchange rate regime change. Reported net income remained low at approximately $2 million, masking the underlying operational strength.

Total revenue for the first half of FY2026 was RMB 196.3 million (note: transcript contains conflicting figures stating both 96.3 and 158.3 in different sections), compared to RMB 158.3 million in the prior year period, reflecting a decline driven by softer consumer spending and strategic discontinuation of third-party merchant relationships. Gross margin remained resilient at approximately 41%, while total operating expenses decreased significantly by 38.8% due to cost discipline and staffing refinements. Net loss narrowed from RMB 100.7 million in the prior year period to RMB 72.4 million, though no guidance was provided for future periods.

Aegon reported first-half FY26 operating results of EUR 804 million (up 9% YoY) and free cash flow of EUR 392 million, driven by a 54% surge in new life sales. However, net result was broadly flat at EUR 608 million due to negative valuation equity impacts from assumption updates totaling EUR 231 million post-tax. Management maintained existing multi-year guidance without raising it despite the strong commercial performance.

Management reported Q2 production of approximately 8,900 ounces from the 30% stake in Manh Choh and reiterated full-year guidance of 40,000-45,000 ounces. The company closed on the Lucky Shot acquisition to remove royalty burdens and remains unhedged on gold, positioning it to capture upside as prices stabilize above $4,000. Cash costs for H1 were $2,665/oz, with expectations of improvement in H2 driven by higher-grade South Pit mining.

Unifi reported Q4 FY26 consolidated net sales of $144.2 million (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $8.2 million, marking a significant turnaround from the prior year's loss. Management highlighted strong performance in Brazil (+17.8%) and improved profitability across all segments following cost-cutting initiatives. However, revenue growth remains constrained by macro headwinds in the Americas (-1% sales) and Asia due to tariff uncertainty.

Deere reported Q3 FY26 net sales of $12.6 billion (up 5%) and EPS of $5.10, beating expectations driven by strong Construction & Forestry growth (+18% YoY) offsetting declines in Production & Precision Ag (-6%). Management raised full-year net income guidance to a range of $4.75-$5 billion but narrowed segment margin outlooks for Agriculture (to 11%-12%) and Construction (to 10.5%-11.5%), citing softening demand in South America, Europe, and tariff headwinds.

Total revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $44.5 million, representing a 29% year-over-year increase driven by product sales of $41.6 million in China. R&D expenses increased to $102.8 million and watching & distribution expenses rose significantly to $33.4 million due to heavy investment in global registration trial enrollment for the two approved products, Lisaftoclax and Olverembatinib. Management reaffirmed its cash runway through 2027 but noted that OpEx is currently at a peak as trials near completion.

Alvotech reported first-half revenue of $212 million and adjusted EBITDA of $46-47 million, both in line with expectations but down significantly year-over-year due to manufacturing slowdowns from facility improvements. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for total revenue between $650-$700 million and adjusted EBITDA between $180-$220 million, noting that the fourth quarter is expected to be strong as supply normalizes following Q2 ramp-up. The company successfully completed a $165 million equity financing in June, bringing cash on hand to approximately $143 million.

Youdao reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 1.5 billion (up 3.5% YoY) and operating profit of RMB 111.5 million (nearly fourfold YoY). Gross margins expanded across Learning Services (+590 bps), Online Marketing Services (+290 bps), while Smart Devices margin contracted due to memory costs but is expected to recover in H2. Management raised guidance for gross margin expansion and reiterated a focus on profitable growth over rapid revenue acceleration.

Net revenues for the second quarter were CNY 1.2 billion, down from CNY 1.64 billion in Q2 FY2025 (approximate YoY decline based on segment breakdowns). Gross margin expanded to 77.1% from 71.4%, while operating profit fell significantly to CNY 130 million compared with CNY 297 million last year due to a sharp contraction in lead generation revenue and higher costs relative to the prior period's scale.

Fourth quarter revenue was $8.2 million (up 25% sequentially but down year-over-year to $6.6M prior Q and significantly below the $16.7M in FY2025), while full-year revenue contracted sharply from $66.4M to $42.1M due to a major customer's capital freeze, tariffs, and higher fuel prices. Gross margin declined sequentially by 10 basis points to 27.4% (from Q3) and fell year-over-year to 30.2%, driven by product mix shifts and lower volumes absorbing fixed costs despite operating expense reductions of $2.6M in the quarter.

Q2 FY2026 net revenue grew 41.4% YoY to RMB 3,419 million driven by a 63.2% surge in retail and hotel network expansion, though gross margins contracted due to mix shifts toward lower-margin supply chain business. Management maintained full-year guidance for total revenue growth at 30%, raised the specific retail segment forecast to +40% YoY based on strong H1 momentum, but reiterated an expectation of a slight decline in full-year net profit margin driven by higher tax rates and continued investment in capability building.

In Q2 FY2026, Daqo New Energy reported revenue of $62.7 million and a net loss attributable to shareholders of $81 million, representing an improvement from the first quarter but still below prior-year levels due to depressed polysilicon prices averaging $4.04/kg against flat production costs of $5.95/kg. Management raised Q3 2026 volume guidance to 40k-45k metric tons and full-year expectations to 160k-180k metric tons, citing a shift toward market-oriented pricing following new anti-involution regulations that prohibit below-cost sales. The company highlighted strong liquidity with $1.9 billion in convertible assets and zero debt while announcing an investment agreement for AIDC power infrastructure equipment expected to generate revenue starting in 2027.

Second quarter net income totaled ARS 206.8 billion (up 39% QoQ), driven by lower loan loss provisions and higher gains on financial instruments at fair value through P&L, though this was partially offset by a foreign exchange loss of ARS 102.1 billion from the bank's net monetary position. Adjusted ROE reached 14.3%, but management revised full-year real loan growth guidance down to a range of 2% to 5%. Asset quality deteriorated with reported NPLs rising to 6.25% and coverage ratios declining, though Stage 3 loans remained well-covered at 95.4%.

BNAI reported Q2 FY2026 results driven by the June 30 completion of its Cataneo acquisition rather than organic revenue growth from existing operations. The company disclosed unaudited pro forma figures for Cataneo (H1 revenue $5.3M) but did not provide specific GAAP revenue or EPS numbers for the quarter in this transcript, noting that detailed results are filed with the SEC. Management emphasized strategic progress and balance sheet strengthening while explicitly stating no timeline exists for recognizing value from joint ventures due to accounting constraints.

Evaxion reported a net loss of $3.7 million for Q2 FY2026 and ended the quarter with DKK 14 million in cash on hand. Management confirmed that operations remain aligned to plan with a maintained cash runway extending into the second half of 2027, supported by an ATM facility recently activated. The company highlighted significant clinical progress across its pipeline, including positive Phase II data for EVX-01 and new preclinical validation for off-the-shelf programs EVX-04 and EVX-05.

Ross Stores reported Q2 FY2027 (Fiscal Year 2026) results with total sales of $6.3 billion (+13% YoY) and comparable store sales growth of 10%. Operating margin expanded by 610 basis points, driven largely by a one-time tariff refund benefit of approximately $253 million ($0.60 EPS). Management raised full-year guidance for earnings per share to the range of $8.61-$8.77 and increased new store opening plans from 110 to 115 locations.

OSI Systems reported Q4 FY2026 revenues of $484 million (down ~4% YoY) and full-year revenue of $1.79 billion ($13M below prior guidance), primarily due to Middle East conflict delays pushing approximately $50 million in Security deliveries into future quarters. Despite the top-line miss, non-GAAP EPS grew 17% year-over-year to a record $3.78 with Q4 adjusted operating margin expanding 200 bps to 17.7%. Management provided fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $1.875-$1.93 billion (up 5%-8.1%) and EPS guidance of $11.13-$11.49, maintaining the prior outlook despite acknowledging conservative assumptions regarding Middle East timing.

ScanSource reported a strong Q4 FY26 with net sales up 17% YoY and non-GAAP EPS of $1.46 (up 43%), driven by broad-based demand across hardware and recurring revenues. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to an organic range of 6%-10%, excluding the impact of a planned MicroAge acquisition expected to close in Q1 FY27, while maintaining adjusted EBITDA expectations between $158M-$165M.

Twin Disc reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $114.4 million (up 18% YoY) and operating income of $7.8 million, driven by strong defense activity and land-based transmission growth. However, gross margins contracted significantly to 26.3%, down from the prior year period due to product mix shifts, tariff dilution, and a one-time favorable adjustment in the previous quarter that is no longer present. Management raised guidance for fiscal 2027 by citing strong backlog levels ($178.3M) and new defense pipeline opportunities.

Alibaba Group reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of CNY 269 billion (up 9% YoY), driven by a 45% acceleration in Alibaba Cloud external revenue and growth in quick commerce. While Adjusted EBITDA decreased 30% to CNY 27.3 billion due to heavy AI infrastructure investments, the company raised its year-end MaaS ARR target confidence (surpassing CNY 16B as of August) and reiterated a long-term goal of $100B external cloud revenue by 2030. Management highlighted strong pricing power in a supply-constrained compute market and narrowed losses in quick commerce, though free cash flow remained negative due to significant CapEx.

Net sales declined year-over-year to $767,000 from $1 million due to the clearance of a legacy backlog in Q4 FY2026 rather than weak demand. Gross profit increased by 29% and gross margin expanded significantly to 30%, driven by higher pricing on new consumer units (Omni One for Quest) compared to lower-priced pre-order shipments delivered previously. Management highlighted strong order growth of 72% year-over-year but noted that defense revenue recognition remains uncertain due to government funding timing, with larger awards likely in FY2028.

LSI reported Q4 FY2026 sales growth of 51% (including 8% organic) and adjusted EBITDA over $25 million (+50%), but the quarter missed internal margin expectations due to lower-margin backlog from the Royston acquisition. Management expects this headwind, estimated at 50-100 basis points, to impact margins for approximately two quarters before clearing by mid-fiscal 2027. Despite the near-term drag on profitability metrics, management reaffirmed its long-term adjusted EBITDA margin target of 12.5% and highlighted strong demand in grocery and petroleum c-store verticals.

Telix reported H1 FY26 revenue of AUD $477 million (up 22% YoY) and EBITDA of AUD $52 million (up 146% YoY), driven by a precision medicine business delivering AUD $390 million in sales. Management maintained full-year guidance for the upper end of its range, citing strong Q2 execution but noting that R&D spend increased to fund late-stage assets like BiPASS and Zircaix.

SQM reported a strong second quarter of FY26 with record quarterly lithium sales volumes exceeding 84,000 metric tons and robust iodine results supported by favorable pricing. Management raised full-year global demand expectations to over 2.1 million metric tons and updated capital expenditure guidance to approximately $3 billion for the 2026-2028 period to support growth initiatives like Salar Futuro. While Q3 lithium prices are expected to be flat, volumes remain strong with a potential upside in Q4.

Second quarter revenue of $178 million beat the top of guidance and grew 25% year-over-year to surpass seasonal peaks early in the year. Adjusted EBITDA reached a quarterly record of $42.4 million (24% margin), exceeding expectations with growth fueled by advertising (+27%) and carrier revenue (+21%). Management raised full-year revenue guidance by adding $2-$5 million above Q2 overperformance, citing strong momentum entering the second half.

Total income declined by 15.5% year-over-year in Q2 FY26 due to a contraction in the Rongyi loan balance and elevated credit costs amidst weak small business demand. While new loan sales grew sequentially (+4.8%) and asset quality metrics improved (CM3 flow rate down, NPL ratio stable), management explicitly stated that net loss continued for the quarter despite sequential narrowing from last year.

Kingsoft Cloud reported Q2 FY26 revenue of RMB 3.07 billion (up 31% YoY), driven by a record AI cloud gross billing of RMB 1.33 billion (+82% YoY). Adjusted operating profit turned positive for the first time with an adjusted margin of 4%, while full-year CapEx guidance remains unchanged at RMB 15 billion despite high quarterly spend.

Datavault reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.7 million, predominantly from its acoustics group, which is significantly below the reiterated full-year target of $200 million and implies a substantial miss against prior expectations for this stage of growth. Management reaffirmed the $200 million annual guidance but noted that significant revenue recognition will occur in Q4 following mid-September exchange launches rather than immediately in Q3. The company highlighted major non-revenue transactions including acquisitions (CyberCatch, BankWyse) and licensing deals with Vivasor/Scilex to strengthen its balance sheet.

For the first half of FY26 (Q1+Q2), iQSTEL reported $207 million in revenue versus approximately $130 million year-ago, representing a 59% increase. The company highlighted that its annualized run rate is now roughly $414 million but explicitly stated this figure should not be considered a forecast for the full fiscal year. Management noted significant margin expansion with gross profit growing from $3.8M to $4.8M and adjusted EBITDA rising from ~$0.2M in Q1 to over $0.7M in Q2, driven by integration synergies.

Ionic Digital reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $48.6 million (up from $37.2M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of $37.6 million, driven by a shift to digital infrastructure leasing with straight-line non-cash recognition rather than cash rent which commenced in August. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $190-$195 million but noted the ERCOT Batch Zero process has paused approval for their Ward County expansion pending verification, pushing expected energization to late 2027.

FLEX LNG reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $106.8 million (excluding EUAs) and net income of $44.9 million ($0.83 EPS), representing a significant improvement over the first quarter but missing prior full-year guidance expectations for revenue growth due to softening spot rates in late summer. Management maintained its full year 2026 guidance, expecting revenues between $345-$370 million and TCE between $73k-$78k per day, citing strong contract coverage of ~89% for remaining available days despite geopolitical disruptions from the Iran conflict reducing Middle East exports.

Webull reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $198.8 million (up 51% YoY) and adjusted operating profit of $62.6 million (up 169% YoY), driven by the successful navigation of the SEC's elimination of the Pattern Day Trader Rule which boosted options volume to a top-five industry position. Adjusted operating margin expanded significantly to 31.5%, while customer assets grew 79% year-over-year to $28.5 billion, with net deposits reaching $1.6 billion.

Beam Global reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $8.6 million, a 21% year-over-year increase and a sharp rebound from the first quarter, driven by backlog conversion and new orders in Europe and drone sectors. Gross margin contracted to 17.8% GAAP (down from 20.3%) due to non-cash depreciation of $700k included in cost of revenues; excluding these items, adjusted gross margin was 26.2%. The company narrowed its net loss to $3.1 million ($0.14/share) compared to a prior year loss of $4.3 million, aided by reduced operating expenses and the absence of last year's goodwill impairment.

Viking reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.2 billion (up 16.5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $748 million (up 18.2% YoY), driven by capacity expansion and higher yields despite low water levels affecting European rivers in July-August. Management noted that Q3 will likely reflect the financial impact of issuing future cruise vouchers to affected guests, with potential margin pressure extending into 2026-2027. The company remains confident in its booking curves for 2027 (53% booked) and fleet expansion strategy.

TOYO reported strong first-half revenue of $261 million (up 87.6% YoY) and Q2 revenue of $118.2 million (up 35% YoY), driven by module sales, though Q2 saw a sequential decline due to lower cell mix. Gross margins expanded significantly in the first half to 32.5%, but management explicitly declined to reaffirm full-year guidance citing near-term uncertainties regarding CBP detentions and Section 232 tariff negotiations.

Second quarter revenue was $47 million, missing the prior guidance of $55 million-$60 million due to a deconsolidation of retail operations and unfavorable product mix. Gross margin declined from 55% in Q2 2025 to 34% in Q2 2026 driven by a higher proportion of low-value trim in the production mix and elevated costs of $122 per pound. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.7 million, significantly below last year's $18.1 million but an improvement from the first quarter loss.

Weibo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $453.8 million (up 2% YoY) and ad revenue of $381 million (down 1% YoY), while value-added services grew to $72.9 million (+19%). Operating income was $125.4 million with a margin of 28%, down from 36% last year due to higher costs, though net margins remained at 23%. Management expressed caution regarding the second half outlook, citing persistent macro headwinds in consumption and advertising budgets for sectors like handsets and e-commerce.

Full Truck Alliance reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of RMB 3.38 billion (up 4.4% YoY) and GAAP-adjusted net income of RMB 1.43 billion (up 6% YoY). Transaction service revenue surged 33.1% to RMB 1.77 billion, driven by a commission network rollout reaching 94.7% penetration across eligible cities. Management raised the platform-wide fulfillment rate record high to 47%, up 2.9 percentage points quarter-over-quarter.

ZTO reported Q2 FY26 revenue of CNY 14.5 billion (up 23% YoY) and adjusted net income of CNY 3.1 billion (up 50.3% YoY), driven by a 6.5% increase in parcel volume to 10.49 billion pieces. Management raised full-year parcel volume guidance to a range of 40.83-42.37 billion, reflecting an updated growth expectation of 6%-10%. Despite rising oil prices adding CNY 0.02 per parcel cost in the quarter, combined unit transportation and sorting costs decreased by CNY 0.02 due to AI-driven efficiency gains.

ADI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.02 billion (up 40% YoY), finishing above the high end of guidance with record earnings per share of $3.45 at the top of expectations. Management raised full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 74%, citing favorable mix, higher fixed cost absorption, and price adjustments driving a sequential expansion despite inflationary pressures.

Toll Brothers delivered a solid beat on both revenue and EPS in Q3 FY26, generating $2.6 billion in home sales revenue (up 4% YoY) and an adjusted gross margin of 25.6%, which exceeded the midpoint of guidance by 35 basis points. Management reaffirmed full-year delivery guidance while narrowing the settlement range to reflect a higher average delivered price between $995,000 and $1 million. The company increased its projected annual share repurchases from $650 million to $700 million.

BILL reported Q4 FY2026 core revenue of $400.5 million (up 16% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 23%. Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance for total revenue ($1.807B-$1.857B, +9%-12%) and EPS ($3.56-$3.79), while explicitly noting headwinds from S&E card acceptance dynamics and go-to-market restructuring that will impact Q1 FY2027.

Coty reported Q4 FY2026 like-for-like sales down 1%, beating the guidance of a mid-single-digit decline and exceeding expectations despite macro volatility. Adjusted EPS came in at breakeven for the quarter (excluding equity swap), while free cash flow reached $348 million, significantly ahead of guidance due to disciplined working capital management. Management provided no full-year FY2027 guidance but forecast Q1 sales declines of low-to-mid-single-digits and EBITDA declines in the low teens as they navigate a transition year involving portfolio simplification and an upcoming Gucci exit.

The company reported a strong beat with organic sales rising 3% and diluted EPS growing 66%, significantly exceeding the initial outlook from August. Operating margins expanded by 320 basis points to reach an annualized run-rate that prompted management to raise their fiscal 2027 operating margin guidance range to 12.7%-13.5%. Management expressed high confidence in accelerating growth for fiscal 2027, citing a diversified portfolio of billion-dollar brands and successful execution across all regions.

Jack Henry reported Q4 FY26 non-GAAP revenue of $633 million (up 7% YoY) and a non-GAAP operating margin of 21%, exceeding prior guidance. Full year fiscal 2026 saw record performance with GAAP EPS of $6.98 (+12%) driven by strong core wins, including the largest new bank client in company history at Woodforest National Bank ($9.2B assets). Management provided FY27 full-year non-GAAP revenue guidance of 6.3%-7.3% and margin expansion of 20-40 bps.

Wolfspeed reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $150 million, meeting the midpoint of guidance and showing a 6% sequential increase driven by AI data center growth which more than doubled from fiscal 2025. Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was -19.9%, reflecting continued underutilization despite product mix improvements, while operating cash flow remained negative at -$54 million due to debt service and R&D investments.

Fiscal Q1 FY27 consolidated delivered sales declined 3% reported (down 1% excluding case goods divestitures) while retail same-store sales slipped slightly despite a strong 16% growth in written sales. Adjusted operating income was $19 million, down from the prior year due to deleverage on lower wholesale and Joybird volume alongside friction costs from strategic investments like plant consolidations. Management provided cautious guidance for Q2 adjusted margins of 4%-5.5%, citing uneven demand patterns and ongoing supply chain transformation expenses.

Lowe's reported Q2 sales of $26 billion (up 8.3% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.40, beating expectations despite a soft comparable sales increase of only 0.2%. Management updated full-year guidance to the low end of the previous range ($92B sales, ~11.6% operating margin), citing elevated fuel/transportation costs offsetting tariff benefits and persistent pressure on DIY demand from weather and macro uncertainty.

Target reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $26.5 billion, representing a 5.3% year-over-year increase driven by a 3.8% rise in comparable sales and traffic growth of 3.6%. Adjusted EPS was $4.11 per share compared to $2.05 last year, with gross margin expanding to 33.7% aided significantly by tariff refunds. Management raised full-year adjusted operating guidance from a range of 4.8%-5.0% to 4.9%-5.1%, citing broad-based strength across demographics and categories.

TJX reported Q2 FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS of $1.22 (up 11% YoY) and consolidated comparable sales growth of 4%, both significantly above plan despite a miss at the Marmaxx division which was attributed to self-inflicted execution issues regarding merchandise mix. Management raised full-year guidance for pre-tax profit margin, gross margin, and EPS, citing strong performance in HomeGoods (7% comp), TJX Canada (6%), and International divisions offsetting the weaker US apparel results.

AEVEX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $201.8 million, representing a 100% year-over-year increase driven by the tactical systems segment and the Deep Strike program. Net income turned positive at $6.7 million compared to a loss in the prior year, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding significantly. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire BlackSea Technologies for up to $650 million and raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a midpoint of $710 million.

DRDGOLD reported exceptional Q4 FY26 results driven by a 40% increase in the gold price and production of roughly 5 tons (approx 1,300 oz), exceeding guidance. Revenue surged to ZAR 11.2 billion (+42%) while operating profit more than doubled to ZAR 4.1 billion for Ergo alone. Management highlighted strong cost discipline despite rising input costs like diesel and carbon, resulting in robust free cash flow of ZAR 2.3 billion.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: ReNew reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of INR 44.6 billion (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 30.4 billion (up 12% YoY), driven by a 26% growth in its operating portfolio to 13.5 GW. Management reiterated full-year FY2027 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance of INR 103-109 billion, maintaining the range despite acknowledging margin contraction in manufacturing and curtailment impacts on solar PLF.

Yalla reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $82.6 million, which beat the upper end of guidance but represented a decline from last year due to geopolitical impacts on paying users. Non-GAAP net margin remained healthy at 41.7% despite doubling watching and marketing expenses YoY. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance broadly in line with expectations while noting potential for updates if new games perform strongly.

Total revenues were RMB 6.3 billion, up 1% sequentially but down year-over-year due to a 4% decline in membership services revenue driven by seasonality and the absence of major hits like 'The Legend'. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed substantially from Q1 (RMB 148.6 million) to RMB 130.3 million, approaching breakeven as AI-driven cost efficiencies began materializing.

Keysight reported record Q3 FY26 results with revenue of $1.846 billion (up 36% YoY) and EPS of $3.70 (up 79%), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Operating margin expanded to 33.2%, up 820 bps, driven by strong core growth in Communications Solutions Group where wireline revenue hit a record billion-dollar quarter for the first time. Management raised full-year and Q4 outlooks citing robust demand across AI infrastructure, defense modernization, and semiconductor markets.

Amer Sports reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 32% (ex-currency) and adjusted EPS of $0.22 vs prior year's $0.06, driven by strong performance across Arc'teryx, Salomon Softgoods, and Wilson Tennis 360 segments with double-digit growth in all regions. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately 24% from the previous 20%-22%, along with increases in adjusted operating margin guidance to 14.2%-14.5%. The quarter featured significant one-time net tariff refund benefits of $64.3 million, which inflated reported margins but management clarified that underlying organic expansion remains robust.

Baidu reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of CNY 31.3 billion, a decrease of 4% year-over-year and 2% quarter-over-quarter, driven by declines in general business (CNY 25.2b) and iQIYI (down 5%). While AI Cloud Infra grew strongly at +50% YoY with GPU cloud revenue surging 283%, the overall miss on top-line growth resulted from pressure in advertising-related segments, leading to a net decline in total earnings.

Total revenues excluding IFRIC 12 grew 8% year-over-year to outpace traffic figures, driven by double-digit growth in Armenia and Brazil despite a decline in Argentina's cargo business due to an exceptionally bad prior-year comparison base. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.5%, with the majority of the miss concentrated in Argentina (down 21%) and Uruguay (down 16%), while four other segments delivered strong double-digit growth. The board approved a $150 million cash dividend for 2026, marking an important milestone in capital allocation.

Einride reported H1 FY26 revenue of EUR 27 million (up 26% YoY), but Adjusted EBITDA widened to a loss of $34.6 million from negative $21 million in the prior year due to increased R&D and IPO preparation costs. Management guided for constant currency revenue growth to double in H2, expecting EUR 39-42 million (driven by Amazon and Tesla Semi ramp), which would result in an annualized run rate of EUR 85-95 million by December. The company reiterated a path to cash flow breakeven in late 2028 with a deployed fleet of 1,500-2,000 vehicles.

Evogene reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $0.3 million compared to $0.5 million in the prior year period, a decrease driven by the conclusion of an agreement with Bayer and lower sales from Casterra. The company's net loss narrowed significantly to approximately $1.8 million from $4.7 million in Q2 2025 due to reduced operating expenses and discontinued operations losses. Management highlighted strategic progress including six active drug development agreements, successful hit-to-lead milestones on two programs, and a reduction in cash burn expectations for the full year.

Hesai Group reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of RMB 861 million (up ~22% YoY), driven by a core LiDAR business generating RMB 816 million and the debut of Strategic Growth Initiatives (SGI) at RMB 45 million. Management raised full-year 2026 SGI revenue guidance from RMB 100 million to RMB 200-300 million, citing faster-than-expected commercialization of robotic actuation modules and Kosmo spatial intelligence platform revenues expected in Q3.

Klarna delivered a strong quarter with revenue of $1.04 billion (up 27%) and transaction margin dollars rising 42% to $446 million, beating the high end of guidance on every line item for two consecutive quarters. Management raised its full-year adjusted operating income outlook by approximately $35-40 million due to stronger unit economics, despite a downward revision to the GMV forecast driven primarily by softer-than-expected consumer sentiment in Germany.

Home Depot reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $47.9 billion (up 5.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.92 (up 5.1%), exceeding expectations driven by a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit that boosted gross margin to 33.7%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, projecting comp sales growth between flat to 2%, with the Q2 tariff windfall expected to be fully offset in Q3 and Q4 by incremental fuel, energy, and commodity cost pressures. While international (Canada/Mexico) and Pro segments showed strength, management noted continued pressure on larger discretionary projects and a frozen housing market.

Pony.ai reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $36.2 million, a 69% year-over-year increase driven by robotaxi revenues reaching a record high of $12.1 million (up 691%) and fare charging revenues surging nearly 8x to over 40%. Operating loss narrowed significantly from -$75M in Q2 FY25 to -$45.4M, with non-GAAP operating expenses growing at only 9.6% while revenue grew by 69%, demonstrating strong operating leverage.

The company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $46.5 million (up 3.9x YoY), with IM8 contributing $45 million at a gross margin expansion to 65%. Management raised full-year total revenue guidance to $220-$230 million and initiated 2027 projections, citing record July performance where CAC fell 21% despite doubled acquisition spend. The business crossed into positive adjusted free cash flow in Q2 due to a new funding facility.

Total revenue decreased by 5.9% to $18.2 million in Q2 FY26 due to macroeconomic headwinds and a significant surge in chip costs affecting the uCloudlink 1.0 business line, while new growth engines like GlocalMe IoT showed strong YoY expansion of 392.4%. Management revised full-year guidance downward from $85M-$100M to $75M-$85M citing persistent macroeconomic challenges and global trade headwinds.

VNET reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 2.78 billion (up 14.2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of RMB 918.3 million (up 25.4% YoY), driven by a robust wholesale IDC business that surpassed the 1 GW capacity milestone in service. Management reiterated full-year guidance for net revenues between RMB 11.5 billion-RMB 11.8 billion and adjusted EBITDA of RMB 3.55 billion-RMB 3.75 billion, maintaining unchanged estimates despite a slight sequential decline in cash gross margin attributed to higher utility pass-through costs.

Flexsteel reported Q4 FY26 net sales of $115.4 million (up 0.7% YoY) and adjusted operating margins of 7.1%, down from the prior year's 9.0%. The quarter included a one-time benefit of tariff refunds but also reflected costs associated with exiting the Homestyles ready-to-assemble category, which contributed roughly $12 million in sales for the fiscal year.

Mercury Systems reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $290 million and full-year organic growth of 7.9%, driven by a massive 93% year-over-year increase in bookings to a new quarterly record of $660 million. Management raised its outlook for FY27, targeting low double-digit organic revenue growth while maintaining an adjusted EBITDA margin profile in the high teens and full-year FCF conversion near 35%. The company highlighted strong domestic demand (up 13%) and expanded backlog visibility to over $1.9 billion.

Vivos Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.2 million, a 35% year-over-year increase driven by service revenue growth from the Sleep Center of Nevada (SCN) acquisition, while product revenue declined due to a strategic pivot away from VIPs. The company incurred a net loss of $5.5 million and ended the quarter with only $1.8 million in cash, explicitly stating that existing funds are insufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months without additional financing. Management highlighted significant headwinds including non-compliance with Nasdaq minimum equity requirements and substantial doubt regarding the company's ability to continue as a going concern.

XP reported Q2 FY26 gross revenue of BRL 5.1 billion (up 8% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 9%, driven by strong corporate segment performance (+32%) despite a challenging fixed income primary market environment that suppressed underlying retail momentum. Management noted the quarter was impacted by mark-to-market losses on investment banking books, estimating roughly BRL 400-420 million in negative impacts compared to prior periods where such effects were lower or absent. While meeting soft guidance targets for net new money and maintaining a robust capital ratio of 20.3%, management adopted a cautious tone regarding future credit growth, emphasizing collateralized lending strategies and conservative risk approaches as they navigate geopolitical volatility.

New Era delivered significant de-risking progress in Q2 FY2026 by securing construction permits and closing the acquisition of a critical land corridor at its flagship TCDC site. The company expanded Phase Two power capacity from 450 MW to approximately 550 MW, bringing total gross capacity for Phases One and Two to roughly 757 MW against previously contemplated levels. Management reaffirmed the target timeline for Phase One delivery in Q4 FY2026 (late 2027 calendar), citing that power availability is now secured via a finalized PPA structure.

In Q2 FY2026, H World Group reported revenue of RMB 7.1 billion (up 10.8% YoY) and adjusted net income of RMB 1.7 billion (up 26.9% YoY). Management maintained full-year guidance for hotel openings despite a slower first half due to supply chain issues, while keeping the full-year RevPAR outlook unchanged amidst macro uncertainties like extreme weather and geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East.

BHP reported strong financial results for FY26 driven by record production in iron ore and Escondida copper amidst resilient prices. The company ended the year with less than $9 billion of net debt and paid a highest-in-four-years dividend of $8.7 billion, though management immediately pivoted to address a fatal incident at Peak Downs mine which halted momentum on safety goals.

Freightos reported record Q2 revenue of $7.7 million (up 3% YoY), driven by a strong platform beat but offset by a solutions decline of 4%. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$2 million due to cost discipline, with cash ending the quarter at $21.4 million. Management raised full-year transaction growth guidance slightly while narrowing revenue expectations and maintaining an adjusted EBITDA breakeven target for Q4.

Q2 FY26 net revenue was approximately $5.6 million (up 2% YoY), while core brands grew 12% and the non-alcoholic/functional segment surged 132%. The company reported a GAAP loss of $7.5M driven by one-time direct listing costs ($4.3M) and intentional inventory write-downs below cost to simplify the portfolio, resulting in compressed gross margins (26.7%). Management provided full-year guidance with net revenues at no less than $18.5 million.

Axe Compute reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.2 million (up from $35k in Q1) and a net loss of $17.2 million driven by $13.1M in unrealized digital asset losses, though adjusted EBITDA was -$4.9M excluding those non-cash items. Management highlighted the signing of over $3 billion in total contract value (TCV), including an incremental $2.9B in H1 Q3, with a projected annualized run rate exceeding $696 million upon full deployment by early 2027. The company announced its first customer prepayment of $317M and signed a new agreement for additional power capacity.

Precipio reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $7 million, a sequential increase from $6.7 million in Q1 and a year-over-year growth of roughly 22% to $5.7 million. The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA with approximately $400,000 (up from -$200,000 in Q1) and generated about $700,000 in operating cash flow while ending the quarter with over $3 million in cash on hand without raising capital. Management highlighted record product revenue of roughly $900,000 driven by a new commercial team and distributor partnerships.

Streamex reported Q2 FY2026 net loss of $14.6 million (down from $46.7M in Q1) and operating expenses reduced by $20.4M due to lower stock-based compensation, while recognizing its first income stream of approximately $134k in gold lease revenue. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated that institutional adoption is expected as a catalyst in the third quarter following recent partnership integrations with Siebert Financial and Inspira Financial. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $41.8M total liquidity, zero debt, and an operating cash burn run rate of approximately $1.1M/month excluding one-time items.

For the nine months ended June 30th, 2026, Sol Strategies reported an EBITDA loss of CAD 1.1 million after adjusting for significant non-cash items including over CAD 6 million in impairment and revaluation losses on its digital asset treasury valued at approximately CAD 48 million. The company acquired Houdini Swap which contributed one month of revenue (CAD 1.2M) but the overall financials reflect a challenging macro environment with volatile crypto markets impacting the balance sheet. Management expressed confidence in long-term growth and team execution despite acknowledging that current market conditions have not yet rewarded their efforts.

Fabrinet reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $1.316 billion (up 45% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.10, both exceeding the top end of guidance. The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 revenue to a record $4.6 billion (+36%) and is entering FY27 with strong momentum across data center, communications infrastructure, and automotive segments. Management highlighted significant capacity expansions in Thailand and Santa Clara to support accelerating demand.

Cosan reported a negative net income of BRL 320 million for Q2 FY2026, showing significant improvement over the prior year but missing profitability expectations due to an impairment charge and seasonality in investee dividends. The company highlighted strategic progress including Compass' IPO proceeds (BRL 2.3 billion), debt prepayments totaling nearly BRL 9 billion reducing expanded net debt by 20% to BRL 9.2 billion, and a projected Debt Service Coverage Ratio range of 0.8x-1.2x for year-end 2026.

HIVE reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $79 million (up 10% q/q and 74% y/y) with earnings from operations growing to $15.2 million despite a net loss driven by non-cash depreciation ($54M) and a Swedish tax provision ($85M). Management highlighted the closing of two major GPU cloud deals adding $95 million in annualized recurring revenue, pushing total contracted HPC ARR past $180 million ahead of their year-end target. The company emphasized strong demand for its compute power and plans to deploy additional capacity via partnerships with Bell Canada.

Duos Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.18 million (up 30% YoY) and net income from continuing operations of $48.7 million following the divestiture of its rail business and a gain on investment sales. The company reconfirmed full-year 2026 guidance to exceed $50M in revenue, citing approximately $17-18M annualized recurring revenue expected by Q4 exit run rate. Management highlighted significant progress in AI infrastructure deployment with new multi-megawatt contracts and a strengthened balance sheet of $112.3 million cash.

Parabolic reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.3 million, a decrease of approximately 16% from the prior quarter and 27% year-over-year due to non-recurring revenue trailing off in legacy products. Net loss narrowed by 41% compared to Q1 driven by cost reductions totaling $1.7M versus Q1, while adjusted EBITDA remained at a loss of $1.7 million. Management raised full-year guidance expectations citing significant second-half growth from ConnectAndSell ($6.5M contribution) and legacy product improvements.

Total revenue was $2.1 million in Q2 FY26, essentially flat sequentially and up 9.8% year-over-year to $1.9 million in the prior period quarter. The company reported a net loss of approximately $4.6 million driven by a $3 million fair value loss on digital assets against an average Bitcoin price decline from ~$75,700 to ~$72,000. Management clarified that previously cited revenue potential figures are illustrative estimates only and not guidance.

RLX Technology reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 1.01 billion (up 14.8% YoY) and gross profit of RMB 357.8 million with a margin expansion to 35.4%. Management noted that sequential revenue moderation was due to trade inventory normalization following Q1 regulatory-driven shipments rather than demand softening, while highlighting the upcoming consolidation of a Western European acquisition in Q3 which will boost reported growth.

Suncrete reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $97.2 million (up 146% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million, but recorded a net loss of $37.1 million due to a $26.9 million non-cash de-SPAC charge. Management maintained full-year guidance for revenue ($420M-$480M), income (net loss of $4M to net income of $20M), and adjusted EBITDA ($68M-$93M). The strong organic growth was achieved despite wet weather conditions in Texas and Oklahoma, with management noting that missed volume is expected to shift into the stronger third quarter.

Sigma Lithium reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $55 million and generated approximately $30-32 million in cash flow from operations for the quarter. While production volumes increased by 52% to 35,400 tons due to a ramp-up that surpassed guidance, revenue was impacted by lower sales volume compared to total production as low-grade material produced but not sold during the quarter is being monetized later. Management adjusted its full-year cost guidance downward based on executed costs of $668/ton and pushed forward certain operational timelines by three months due to a temporary suspension related to TAC negotiations.

Braskem reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated recurring EBITDA of $1.043 billion with a margin of 24%, driven by significant international spread increases (up to 73% in Mexico) and PIS/COFINS credits, partially offset by lower Brazilian sales volumes and currency appreciation. Management noted that the strong quarter was largely tactical due to Middle East conflict-induced supply shocks rather than structural demand growth, with spreads expected to normalize toward pre-conflict levels in Q3. The company emphasized a focus on capital structure restructuring and operational discipline as it navigates global overcapacity.

Nuvve reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.23 million, a 268% year-over-year increase driven by V2G school bus charging station deliveries and Japan interconnection services. However, margins contracted significantly to -14.5% excluding grants due to a $1.2 million Troy project write-down and higher warranty costs on DC chargers. The company is trading on the OTCQB following NASDAQ delisting for failing listing standards but maintains an immediate priority to return to a senior market within months.

Sinda reported its first quarter as a public company following the successful IPO which secured $331 million in gross proceeds and strategic investments from Fresnillo and Franco-Nevada. The Company completed Phase One surface drilling of nearly 61,000 meters across Caracol, Agaves, and Don Diego targets without any revenue or EPS to report as it remains a pre-production exploration stage asset. Management raised guidance for total annualized drilling by year-end from the initial plan of ~128,000m (based on Phase 1 + planned Phase 2) to nearly 135,000 meters after accelerating Phase Two plans.

Corvex reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.8 million entirely from its newly integrated AI platform business following a March merger with Corvex Legacy Holdings; the legacy healthcare segment was fully wound down and transferred to lenders, resulting in no meaningful year-over-year comparisons. Management highlighted that contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached approximately $22 million as of August 4th, driven by new cluster deliveries including Blackwell expansion funded via debt financing and customer prepayments. The quarter included significant non-cash stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) related to merger equity awards and disclosed unremediated material weaknesses in internal controls.

Total revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $45.5 million driven by services and OTC growth, while exchange revenue declined 38% due to soft crypto volumes. Net loss narrowed slightly to $107.7 million from a prior quarter's adjusted EBITDA deterioration of roughly $26M compared to Q1, primarily reflecting non-cash mark-to-market losses on Bitcoin holdings following the May strategic investment. Management provided no formal revenue guidance for 2H but expects technology and G&A expenses between $155m-$170m full year.

Super League reported Q2 FY26 gross revenue of approximately $3 million (flat YoY and sequentially) with net revenue increasing to ~$1.24M (+16% seq). Gross margin expanded to 41%, while Adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of ~$1.7M, improving from the prior year quarter but missing profitability targets for H1. Management reaffirmed guidance for adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 and highlighted pipeline growth driven by new sales leadership and Misfits integration.

Firy reported Q2 FY26 GAAP revenue of $31 million (up 23% YoY), but the company posted a net loss of $24.5 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $13.6 million, including approximately $11 million in litigation expenses. While RZR achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability with strong growth, Skillz revenue declined sequentially due to operational headwinds and reduced user acquisition spend aimed at fixing funnel issues. Management highlighted a recent court victory awarding ~$730 million against Papaya Gaming but noted that proceeds are not yet realized in financial statements.

Revenue grew 12.8% year-over-year to $3.6 million in Q2 FY2026, driven by a 42% increase in cut herb sales and expanded relationships with major retailers like Target and Kroger. SG&A expenses declined significantly by approximately $0.9 million (21.5%) compared to the prior year period as management focused on operational efficiency. The company made significant progress on its Prairie Hills manufacturing platform, completing prototype production at Tetra Pak's facility while securing pre-sold commitments for 100% of future capacity.

Digi Power X reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $6.6 million and a net loss of $14.4 million, driven by the transition to AI compute revenue which began in May with only five weeks of income from GPU rentals. While adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $3.3 million (up $3.2m YoY), management highlighted significant balance sheet improvements including cash rising to ~$150M and total assets reaching $279M, but explicitly stated that the company is still in debt financing discussions rather than having secured a facility yet.

Cemig reported Q2 FY26 operating performance of BRL 2.5 billion and recurring EBITDA growth of 9.3% YoY, though net income was impacted by higher financial expenses from funding investments for the program totaling BRL 4.6 billion in the quarter. The company is executing its investment plan with BRL 1.8 billion CapEx (BRL 2.6 billion in distribution) and expects a tariff review impact of +6.5% average starting May 2028, while acknowledging trading losses of -BRL 180 million due to position settlements that were expected but offset by generation results.
