Sidus Space reported a significant revenue miss for the second quarter of FY2026 with total Q2 revenue declining to approximately $583,000 from $1.3 million in the prior year period (a decrease of 54%). While net loss narrowed due to non-operating factors like loan repayment and higher interest income, operating performance deteriorated as gross profit before depreciation declined by approximately $117,000 and cash operating expenses increased by roughly $1 million.

BTQ reported Q2 FY2026 with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted product milestones including a CAD$150M ATM launch and over $9.73 million cash on hand, but explicitly stated that commercial contracts for key products like QSSN are still under negotiation with expected monetization only starting in H2 2026. The company acknowledged significant delays to IP release timelines due to new AI-driven cryptographic threats requiring additional security analysis, and noted the recent integration of QPerfect is self-funding via grants rather than immediate revenue generation.

Americas Gold and Silver reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $46.3 million (up 71% YoY) driven by a silver price increase to $67/oz, while consolidated production reached ~800k silver equivalent ounces with Cosalá output up 26%. The company settled remaining variable delivery obligations for Sprott and Royal Gold, removing over $76 million in future debt service. Management reiterated full-year guidance of 3.2-3.6M oz despite Q2 being a trough quarter due to infrastructure spending at Galena.

Second quarter revenue was approximately $0.4 million, flat year-over-year compared to Q1's growth but lower than the prior period due to timing in services and deferred recognition from a vet agreement. Operating expenses decreased by 32% YoY following headcount reductions, yet net loss widened slightly to $7.3 million driven by non-cash charges on convertible notes. Management explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for FY2026 citing the lumpy nature of project delivery and deferred revenue recognition.

Aya reported Q2 FY2026 production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), a 61% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter rise, driven by record performance at the Zgounder mine where mining rates reached 4,900 tonnes per day against a plant nameplate capacity of 2,700 tonnes. Revenue surged to $97 million (up 151% YoY) and net income hit $35 million due to strong cash costs ($17.69/oz at Zgounder) despite silver prices averaging below the quarter's low-water mark. Management confirmed full alignment with H1 guidance for production, cash cost, and CapEx while highlighting a successful Nasdaq listing as a major catalyst.

Credicorp reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with a 20.3% ROE and accelerated loan growth of 13.1%, driven by retail banking at BCP and Mibanco despite El Niño-related provisions adding 27 bps to the cost of risk. Management raised its medium-term ROE expectation from 19.5% to approximately 22% citing structural improvements, while reaffirming full-year loan growth guidance around 12%. The company remains confident in Peru's economic outlook and expects fee income to grow into the high teens.

Total revenue for Q2 FY26 reached $40.4 million, beating the high end of guidance and growing 18% year-over-year to a third consecutive quarter of accelerating growth. GAAP net profit was $2.2 million (up 50%), though gross margin contracted slightly to 63.7% due to product mix changes as Conversational AI usage grew at a subscale stage. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance expectations, projecting between $41M and $42M with growth of 15.8%-18.6%, while reaffirming the goal of achieving GAAP operating profitability by year-end.

AirJoule Technologies reported a net loss of $8.5 million for Q2 FY26, driven by non-cash losses on earn-out shares and an increase in full-year cash spend guidance to approximately $27-$28 million from the prior expectation. Management highlighted significant commercial milestones including an exclusive partnership with Kubota Corporation for residential development in Texas and California, a deployment at GE Vernova's Frontier Campus, and regulatory validation via UAE green licenses.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $31.1 million (up ~270% YoY), but the company reported a GAAP net loss of $75 million and an operating loss of $12.9 million, heavily impacted by one-time non-cash items including a $55.7M tax charge from transitioning to C-Corp status and $64.4M in other transaction-related adjustments. Management reaffirmed guidance for approximately $400 million annualized recurring revenue at year-end 2026 but provided no specific EPS or margin targets due to the one-time nature of the quarter's results.

Q2 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to $1.92 million driven by a 53% increase in license fees, but the quarter missed proposed expectations due to a delayed hardware shipment shifting into H2. Gross margin expanded significantly to 87%, while net loss improved 51% to $0.56 per share on an adjusted basis of shares post-reverse split. Management targets profitability for the second half of 2026, citing strong pipeline growth in EMEA and new AI governance opportunities.

Parabolic reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.3 million, a decrease from the prior year quarter and down significantly due to non-recurring revenue trailing off in legacy products. The company acquired ConnectAndSell which will contribute approximately $15M annually starting later this year but is not reflected in current results. Net loss improved 41% YoY to $5 million driven by cost reductions, though the business remains unprofitable with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.7 million.

NET Power reported Q2 FY2026 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted a strategic recalibration to prioritize unabated natural gas power generation over carbon capture due to immediate grid constraints and market demand for speed. The company redirected capital focus toward behind-the-meter solutions while preserving long-term optionality for CCS, citing $310 million cash on hand but noting that project financing remains required.

Azul reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenue of BRL 5 billion (up 0.7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 510 million in a seasonally weak quarter impacted by fuel prices up 61%. Management declined to provide full-year guidance due to extreme volatility in the fuel curve, noting that capacity was reduced proactively by 10.6% to protect liquidity while maintaining record RASK.

For Q3 FY2026, Outlook Therapeutics reported an adjusted net loss of $10.9 million ($0.09/share), a significant improvement from the prior year's $15.8 million loss and last quarter's unit sales decline in Europe which saw a 46% increase but remains below breakeven territory overall. Management provided forward guidance for total U.S. net revenue of $50-$75 million over the first 12 months following launch, with SG&A expenses expected to double by end-2026 and R&D remaining steady as they prepare for a commercial launch later this year.

Net sales for the fiscal third quarter totaled $3.4 million, representing a 27% year-over-year increase driven by Halo's operational improvements and supply chain recovery reaching 98%. GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $4.1 million, an improvement of 40% year-over-year to a smaller absolute loss compared to the prior period. Management highlighted a debt-free balance sheet with no repurchases made under the newly authorized program due to blackout periods.

CAE reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenues of CAD 1.2 billion (up 6.8% YoY), while adjusted segment operating income declined to CAD 156.6 million (-7.5%) and EPS remained flat at CAD 0.26 due to higher SG&A, credit charges in Civil, and defense bid costs. Management maintained its full-year fiscal 2027 outlook unchanged despite the quarter's mixed results, citing expected seasonality impacts on Civil margins later in the year. The company generated strong free cash flow of CAD 104 million and repurchased shares.

Tapestry reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 11% and EPS of $1.32 (up 28%), exceeding expectations despite a higher tax rate headwind. The company achieved its three-year commitments two years ahead of plan, delivering record results with operating margin expansion to over 23%. Management raised the dividend by 16% and maintained full-year FY27 guidance for mid-single-digit revenue growth.

Applied Industrial Technologies reported a solid finish to fiscal Q4 FY26 with record sales of $1.3 billion (up 10% YoY) and EPS of $3.17 (up 13%). EBITDA margins expanded by over 60 bps to 13%, driven by volume growth in automation and fluid power, though gross margin was slightly down due to LIFO expense. Management raised intermediate financial targets for fiscal 2028-2029, increasing the sales objective to $7 billion from $5.5 billion and EBITDA margins to 14%.

EnerSys reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $936 million (up 5% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.20 per share (excluding one-time tariff refunds), driven by strong growth in Network Infrastructure Solutions (+9%) and Precision Power Solutions (+24%). Management raised second-quarter guidance, expecting revenue between $955-$995 million and excluding-45X adjusted EPS up 21% YoY at the midpoint. The company highlighted record free cash flow of $218 million and secured a DOE grant for a new defense-focused lithium manufacturing facility.

McGraw Hill reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $550 million (up 2.6% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $207 million with a margin expansion to 37.7%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, citing strong momentum in K-12 ELA adoption driven by the science-of-reading mandates and higher education share gains despite awaiting final enrollment data for H2 visibility.

Kimball Electronics reported Q4 FY26 net sales of $371.6 million, a 2% year-over-year decline and a sequential increase, with adjusted operating income at $18.1 million (4.9% margin). The company raised full fiscal 2027 guidance to organic revenue growth of 3%-5%, projecting total FY27 sales between $1.535 billion and $1.56 billion driven by medical segment expansion, while acknowledging automotive will likely be flattish due to EV demand softness.

For fiscal Q4 FY26, MSG Sports reported total revenues of $278.7 million and adjusted operating income (AOI) of $39.6 million, representing a significant beat against the prior year's revenue of $204 million and AOI loss of -$16.8 million driven by Knicks championship playoffs. Management raised full-year FY26 guidance to approximately $59 million in AOI from an implied lower range based on Q4 results but declined to provide specific numerical guidance for fiscal 2027, citing higher team compensation and revenue sharing expenses as headwinds.

FocalTherics reported Q2 FY26 HIFU revenue of $13.2 million, a 39% year-over-year increase driven by 13 capital system sales and strong procedure volume growth in the U.S. Gross margin expanded to 55.6%, while operating expenses rose due to strategic investments and non-cash warrant charges. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for core HIFU revenue between $50 million-$54 million, maintaining their previously announced targets despite a change in financial reporting classification.

Bit Digital reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $32.1 million (up 15% sequentially) and a net loss attributable to shareholders of $107.2 million ($0.31 EPS), driven by an $86 million non-operating charge from digital asset revaluation, impairment on liquid staked ETH for financing collateralization, interest expense, and derivative losses. Management highlighted strong operating cash flow growth but noted the market continues to value the company as a passive treasury despite active capital allocation strategies like WhiteFiber expansion and bridge financing.

Bending Spoons reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $704 million (up 126% YoY) and adjusted operating income of $381 million (up 150%), driven by strong performance in AOL Advertising, WeTransfer, and Tractive. Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $2.78 billion-$2.82 billion and adjusted operating income between $1.46 billion-$1.51 billion, which excludes the pending Airtable acquisition expected to close later this year.

Aebi Schmidt reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $496 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $42 million (up 22% YoY), driven by a backlog increase to ~$1.3 billion and strong performance in North America and Europe. Management confirmed full-year guidance for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA, noting that realized synergies are accelerating toward the updated target of over $40M annually while acknowledging temporary supply chain investments impacting leverage targets slightly into 2027.

AIRO reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.2 million (up ~76% YoY) and swung to a small operating profit of $1.7M from a prior year loss, driven by drone segment outperformance where gross margins expanded to 64%. Management reiterated full-year revenue growth guidance of 15%-25%, noting that H1 represented roughly half of current annual expectations due to timing shifts in major deliveries and anticipated FX headwinds.

Alliance Laundry reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 7% YoY and adjusted EBITDA growth of 12%, driven by pricing power that offset inflationary pressures including tariffs. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA to an 8%-10% range while maintaining the prior revenue outlook, citing strong first-half performance and visibility into H2 demand despite minor regional lumps in Middle East/Africa.

AmpliTech Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $8.1 million (up 51% sequentially but down year-over-year) and a net loss of roughly $3.09 million driven by elevated investments in R&D, marketing, supply chain readiness, and cybersecurity to support larger customers. Gross margin improved significantly from the prior year period due to product mix changes following an asset acquisition, rising from 7.8% YoY but declining sequentially from Q1's 48%. Management explicitly declined to reaffirm or provide specific revenue guidance for the remainder of FY2026, citing timing uncertainties in large telecom deployments.

Total revenue reached $1.3 billion (up >14% YoY in USD), with adjusted EBITDA of $126.8 million representing a record quarter and more than 20% growth versus last year's second quarter. The company delivered its highest ever quarterly net income, driven by margin expansion in Brazil (+70 bps excluding FX) and strong digital sales penetration (>25% YoY). Management raised the bar for expectations citing resilience despite challenging consumer dynamics.

Ascendis Pharma reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of EUR 339 million (up from EUR 145m in the prior quarter), driven by YORVIPATH sales of EUR 252 million and SKYTROFA at EUR 55 million. The company achieved a significant non-product milestone gain of EUR 17 million related to TransCon CNP, resulting in net profit of EUR 207 million. Management raised full-year cash flow guidance expectations from greater than EUR 300m (implied prior) to greater than EUR 500 million for the remainder of 2026.

Birkenstock reported Q3 FY26 revenue of EUR 720 million (up 15% in constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA of EUR 242 million. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to the high end of its range at 15% and increased the minimum adjusted EBITDA target to at least EUR 710 million, citing strong momentum across all regions despite FX headwinds and tariffs.

Aveanna Healthcare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $670 million (up 13.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $95.4 million (up 8% YoY), driven by volume growth across all segments including a 14.8% increase in Home Health & Hospice. Management raised full-year guidance to revenue greater than $2.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA greater than $365 million, citing improved rate environments and successful preferred payer execution.

Grupo Aval reported Q2 FY26 attributed net income of COP 577 billion (up 17% YoY) and ROAE of 12.7%, driven by loan/deposit growth and strong investment portfolio contributions. Management maintained full-year ROAE guidance at 9.25% despite a first-half performance near 10%, citing caution regarding second-half NIM pressures from further rate hikes, earthquake impacts on asset quality, and potential local tax increases in Bogotá.

HeartBeam reported a net loss of $5 million for Q2 FY2026, which included approximately $1 million in one-time items related to leadership transition and severance; excluding these, the underlying operating cash outflow decreased by roughly 7% quarter-over-quarter. Management confirmed that initial commercial orders have shipped with patients being onboarded at concierge practices across four U.S. geographies (New York, Dallas, South Florida, Southern California), though specific revenue figures were not disclosed as the business remains in a learning stage. The company submitted its pre-submission to the FDA today for heart attack detection indication via the 510(k) pathway.

Second quarter revenue grew 10.6% to $23.4 million with gross margin expanding 445 bps to 51.9%, but GAAP EPS of $0.79 missed the prior year's $0.96 due primarily to a $560,000 increase in income tax provision and higher SG&A expenses driven by R&D investments. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue of at least $90 million and non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $3.55 despite the sequential decline in profitability metrics.

Q2 FY2026 revenue increased 57% year-over-year to $2.6 million while net loss declined by 24% from the prior quarter and cash burn decreased to $1.7 million. Management highlighted a shift toward higher-margin non-QM products, resulting in July margins reaching company records and sequential improvements across operating expenses and adjusted EBITDA. However, management explicitly stated they are not providing formal financial guidance for Q3 due to market uncertainty.

Bullish reported Q2 FY26 adjusted revenue of $92.6 million (up 62% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 32%, though trading volumes moderated with the broader crypto market decline. Management narrowed its full-year SSNO guidance to a range of $225-$245 million due to increased visibility into the softer price environment, while maintaining optimism about long-term tokenization opportunities post-acquisition closing in January 2027.

Belite Bio reported a GAAP net loss of $28.4 million in Q2 FY26 compared to $16.3 million last year, driven by R&D expenses rising from $11M to $18.2M due to phase III milestone royalties and SG&A increasing from $6.5M to $16.7M due to team expansion. The company ended the quarter with $780 million in cash equivalents but provided no revenue guidance as it remains pre-commercial, focusing entirely on FDA approval for tinlarebant by February 2027.

Distributable earnings before realizations increased 15% year-over-year to $1.4 billion in the quarter ($0.61 per share), while total distributable earnings including realizations reached $1.5 billion or $0.66 per share. The company reported record fundraising of $77 billion and completed strategic initiatives including the acquisitions of Oaktree and Just Group, alongside a simplification transaction approved by shareholders. Management highlighted strong leasing momentum with net rents 25% above expiring levels in the U.S., though they noted patience on pension pricing due to current market rates.

Innovative Aerosystems reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $26.7 million (up ~11% YoY) and net income of $4.5 million ($0.25 diluted EPS), driven by strong organic growth in commercial/business aviation excluding a difficult F-16 comparison. Gross margin expanded to 51.7%, the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%. Management raised guidance for Q4 revenue to $28-$30M and highlighted strategic wins including an eVTOL contract win, Aydin acquisition integration, and inclusion in the Russell 2000 Index.

SOLV Energy reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $951 million (up 77% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $117 million, contributing to record first-half results with total H1 revenue near $1.63 billion. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue ($3.87B-$3.97B), adjusted gross profit ($620M-$660M), and adjusted EBITDA ($485M-$505M) citing strong execution, project acceleration, and the recent Roberson Waite acquisition closing on July 1st.

Applied Materials reported record Q3 FY26 revenue of $9.1 billion (up 15% sequentially and 25% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS of $3.50 (up 41% YoY). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, citing strengthened demand visibility from customers providing eight-quarter rolling forecasts through to 2030. The company expects particularly strong growth in DRAM and leading-edge foundry logic for the second half of calendar 2027.

Karyopharm reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $33.4 million (down from $37.9M prior year) and a net loss of $67 million due to the conclusion of Menarini's reimbursement, though underlying operating performance improved with disciplined expense reductions. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue between $130-$150 million but highlighted an urgent liquidity constraint requiring financing or strategic alternatives by September 10th to avoid a default on their term loan.

Globant reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $614.4 million, which was within the prior guided range but represented a slight year-over-year decline and sequential growth of only 1.2%. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance downward to a range of $2.43B-$2.46B from the previous $2.46B-$2.51B, citing geopolitical pressures in new markets (specifically Middle East) and travel sector slowdowns due to oil prices. Adjusted operating margin slipped below expectations to 13.2% as FX headwinds impacted Colombia and utilization targets were missed.

GMR Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.49 billion (3.3% YoY growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $285 million, which was down 11.8% YoY due to a lack of favorable No Surprises Act estimate adjustments compared to the prior year. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $5.89B-$6.18B and adjusted EBITDA between $1.135B-$1.195B, noting that underlying performance remains strong despite headwinds from ACA subsidy expiration impacts of approximately $16 million per quarter.

HawkEye 360 reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $49.8 million (up 87% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $7.0 million, driven by the acquisition of ISA but offset by a decline in legacy U.S. business due to government shutdowns. The company completed its IPO with net proceeds of approximately $437.5 million and ended the quarter with $292 million in backlog. Full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($215M-$220M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($30M-$36M) was provided, though no specific prior period guidance figures were explicitly compared to determine a raise or cut.

HeartFlow reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $64.1 million, up 48% year-over-year and ahead of expectations, driven by accelerating plaque adoption and durable FF-CT utilization. Management raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to a range of $246-$250 million (representing 40%-42% growth) and increased the non-GAAP gross margin outlook to approximately 82%. The company highlighted record new account additions in Q2, with plaque activations ahead of plan and coverage reaching roughly 78%.

Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY26 was $1 million (up from $0.5M last year), while the net loss widened to $34.9 million and adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $22.6 million. Management suspended consolidated positive cash flow targets for 2028 due to delays in Accelsius reaching breakeven, citing constraints on power availability and GPU access that are sidelining smaller early adopters like DarkNX. Consequently, the company is suspending specific revenue guidance until market adoption dynamics shift.

ITG reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 38% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA up 21%, both ahead of plan despite slower core infrastructure deployment activity driven by weather timing. Management provided full-year guidance expecting mid-30s top-line growth (approx $1.5B-$1.6B) and margin expansion in the back half as startup costs abate, though they did not raise specific prior guidance figures but rather confirmed a strong outlook consistent with IPO expectations.

Jefferson Capital reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $178 million (up 16% YoY) and collections of $301 million (up 18% YoY), driven by strong deployments including a record July figure. Adjusted EPS was $0.77, with cash efficiency at 72.2%. The company raised its estimated remaining collections to $3.4 billion (+18%) but did not provide specific forward guidance for revenue or earnings.

JD.com reported Q2 FY26 total revenues of RMB 346 billion, a slight year-on-year decline of 2.9% due to high comparison bases in electronics and home appliances. Non-GAAP net income surged by 20.8% YoY to RMB 8.9 billion as JD Retail gross margin expanded to 18.5% and JD Food Delivery losses narrowed significantly. Management raised the outlook for H2, expecting top-line growth re-acceleration in electronics/home appliances once base effects normalize.

KinderCare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $698 million, down slightly from the prior year's $700 million and missing expectations due to a 4% decline in total enrollment driven by footprint optimization. Adjusted EPS was $0.08 compared to $0.22 last year, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $63 million as management updated full-year guidance downward to reflect the impact of closing approximately 80-85 centers and a reduced tuition contribution assumption from state subsidies.

Q2 revenue was $2.1 million and down significantly from the prior year due to supply chain delays and a new Texas facility not yet contributing; gross margins resulted in a loss for the quarter as planned shipments were delayed. Management exited Bitcoin mining, repaid its credit facility using proceeds from watching 333 Bitcoin, and simplified operations by terminating mining agreements while focusing resources on KULR ONE.

Nektar Therapeutics reported Q2 FY26 non-cash royalty revenue of $10.1 million and a net loss of $40.6 million ($1.23 per share). Management raised full-year cash guidance to end at approximately $815-$840 million, extending the runway into late 2028 past mid-2028 data readouts. The company initiated its Phase III ZENITH AD program in July and received FDA alignment for a single registrational study (ZENITH AA) in alopecia areata to be initiated in early 2027.

Legence reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.3 billion (up 111% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 114%, driven by organic expansion in data centers/technology and the Bowers acquisition. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue ($4.7B-$4.8B, up ~13%) and adjusted EBITDA (~$565M-$585M, up ~20%), citing strong backlog growth of $5.7 billion (up 105% YoY) and accelerating project execution speeds.

Lucid Diagnostics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.5 million (up ~17% sequentially) on a test volume of 2,770 units that remained within the targeted range but did not beat prior quarter levels due to pending Medicare reimbursement status. Management highlighted significant progress in commercial coverage with Concert and VA contracting milestones while noting cash burn remains elevated at $11.3 million per quarter as they build infrastructure ahead of expected Medicare approval.

Intuitive Machines reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $206 million (up from a loss in the prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of -$14 million (improving from -$25 million). The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for revenue between $900M-$1B and positive adjusted EBITDA, citing record backlog growth to $1.8 billion driven by diversification into commercial GEO satellites ($600M award) and national security programs (SDA Tranche 3/AMDT3). Management noted that near-term cash usage remains elevated due to strategic inventory investments but expects free cash flow improvement in the second half of the year.

Lifeway Foods reported record quarterly net sales of $66.9 million in Q2 FY2026, representing a 24.1% year-over-year increase and extending its streak to 27 consecutive quarters of growth. However, gross margin contracted significantly to 19.5%, primarily due to elevated milk prices, packaging resin costs, and transportation pressures related to the Middle East conflict. Management noted that while SG&A decreased as a percentage of sales (operating leverage), near-term profitability remains under pressure from these input cost headwinds.

Midera reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $245 million (up 13% YoY) and estimated standalone adjusted EBITDA of $41.8 million, beating the high end of prior guidance by including ~$8m in public company costs. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance midpoints for both revenue ($935-$965M) and EBITDA ($160-$176M), citing strong backlog health and organic demand despite tariff headwinds. The quarter included a record $446 million backlog, up 51% YoY.

Group-wide adjusted property EBITDA was $304 million in Q2 FY26, down from the prior year due to a negative impact of approximately $9 million at City of Dreams Macau driven by an unfavorable VIP win rate that declined from 3.9% YoY to 2.7%. Management noted lower than expected visitation and hold relative to prior quarters placed pressure on margins in Macau, though international properties showed resilience with Manila EBITDA up 9% and Cyprus rising 60%. For the remainder of FY26, total depreciation is guided at $140-$145 million while OpEx per day remains steady at approximately $3.4 million.

Mobilicom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $1.2 million driven by a shift to monthly delivery cadence under the U.S. Marine Corps program of record. The company maintains an EBITDA loss of roughly half a million USD per month, funded by a strong balance sheet with nearly $16 million in cash and no debt. Management highlighted progress on design wins for new products like SkyHopper Multiband but noted that backlog is lower than the prior quarter due to increased throughput.

M-tron reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $15.1 million (up 13.8% YoY) and net income of $1.9 million ($0.43 diluted EPS), though GAAP gross margins contracted to 41.2% from 43.6%. Management noted a one-time non-cash stock-based compensation charge in the current quarter but expects guidance for H2 FY2026 gross margins between 41.5%-44%, citing margin pressure as new programs ramp up.

Merlin reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $2.2 million (up from $1M in Q1) and a GAAP net loss of $58.4 million, which improved by $32M compared to the prior quarter due to non-cash financing items; adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $27.8 million versus a loss of $23.3 million previously as engineering investment continued. Management highlighted significant technical milestones including CDR completion on the C-130J and SOI 3 certification with New Zealand, but explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for FY2026 or beyond, citing reliance on future contract expansions.

Golar LNG reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenue of $130 million and EBITDA of $127 million (up ~20% q/q), driven by Hilli's commodity-linked earnings which rose to $37M from $10M in the prior quarter. The company announced a firm order for its fourth FLNG unit, securing an option for a fifth at CIMC and signing an LOI with Seatrium for further growth units. Management highlighted strong operational performance including 15% overproduction on Gimi and 100% economic uptime on Hilli.

GDS Holdings reported a record first-half of FY26 with 470 MW in new bookings and secured an additional 600 MW in reservations for future needs. Management raised its full-year sales target to 1 GW from the prior guidance, alongside raising CapEx paid guidance from RMB 9 billion to RMB 10 billion. Pro forma adjusted EBITDA growth is now implied at 6.5% for FY26 following pro-forma adjustments that deduct one-time items and restructured recurring income.

Forum Markets reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.4 million and a net loss narrowing to $12.4 million from the prior quarter's $77.5 million loss due to asset sales and buybacks rather than operational growth. Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $18-$22 million, driven by aircraft lease income ($5-6M in H2) and a pending AI compute deal expected to contribute ~$8-12M in Q4. The company executed significant share repurchases (7.1M shares), reducing outstanding equity by 35%.

Fermi America delivered a milestone quarter by securing a binding agreement with TensorWave for up to 650 MW of capacity (initially 222 MW) representing approximately $6.5 billion in revenue over the initial term, alongside an upsized convertible notes offering that strengthened liquidity and appointed Lee McIntire as CEO effective immediately. The company executed all five objectives of its 90-day plan, including securing EPC partnerships with Primoris and TSK, forming a strategic alliance with Hillcore to add 2.6 GW of incremental power capacity by 2028, and delivering major on-site milestones like the arrival of Siemens turbines at Port of Houston.

Blaize reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $12 million (up from $2.7M prior quarter) but significantly reduced its full-year 2026 guidance to a range of $40-43 million, down from the previous expectation of ~$130 million. The revision was driven by failed commercial conversions despite successful pilots, customer order deferrals in regions like the Middle East and US, and material increases in memory pricing that eroded margins to 8% for the quarter (down from Q1's 58%). Management maintains a backlog of approximately $70-90 million secured via signed agreements but expects only partial revenue recognition this year.

Capricor reported zero revenue and a net loss of $40.7 million ($0.70 per share) for Q2 FY26, driven by increased operating expenses of $42.9 million as the company continues to invest in its deramiocel program despite regulatory setbacks. The FDA Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted against approval for the cardiomyopathy indication (3-9), though management plans to resubmit an amended BLA focusing on upper limb skeletal muscle efficacy supported by HOPE-3 data published in The Lancet. Commercial readiness activities are being paced until regulatory clarity is achieved.

Innovative Aerosystems reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $26.7 million (up ~11% YoY) and net income of $4.5 million ($0.25 diluted EPS), driven by strong organic growth in commercial/business aviation excluding a difficult F-16 comparison. Gross margin expanded to 51.7%, the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance expectations (implied beat) and highlighted significant strategic wins including an eVTOL contract win, Aydin acquisition integration progress, and inclusion in the Russell 2000 Index.

Management provided no specific financial results for Q2 FY2026 in this transcript, instead focusing on strategic updates regarding their convertible debt structure and capital stack simplification. They maintained a long-term target of one SOL per share by December 2028 but explicitly downgraded precision on short-term guidance due to market volatility. The company highlighted Solana network upgrades like Alpenglow and increased TPS while noting that preferred equity issuance is currently gated by low SOL prices.

Celcuity reported a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $78.9 million ($1.44/share) and an adjusted net loss of $58.7 million ($1.07/share), representing significant year-over-year deterioration in profitability driven by a $35 million increase in SG&A expenses to support commercial launch preparations. While the company achieved major regulatory milestones including FDA approval for REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) and positive Phase III data, it has not yet generated any revenue from product sales as shipments are expected only late in Q3 2026.

Cellebrite reported Q2 FY26 ARR of $508 million (up 21%) and revenue of $131 million (up 16%), but missed the bottom end of guidance due to delayed large transactions involving cloud/AI procurement requirements. Management lowered full-year ARR guidance by approximately $15 million at the midpoint, citing moderation in Insights conversions and elongated sales cycles for federal deals requiring new permits like FEPs. Conversely, adjusted EBITDA targets were raised to reflect continued cost discipline despite lower revenue expectations.

For the second quarter of FY2026 ending June 30, Co-Diagnostics reported total revenue of $166,000 compared to $163,000 in the prior year period. The company achieved a significant regulatory milestone by submitting its Dual 510(k) and CLIA Waiver for an upper respiratory assay but continues to operate at low revenue levels with net losses narrowing from $7.7 million to $6.3 million due to reduced operating expenses.

CorMedix reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of $101.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $58.7 million, significantly beating the prior year period which included no Melinta contribution. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance at $325-$345 million while raising full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a new range of $125-$140 million following a multi-year commercial supply agreement with an additional large dialysis organization.

Q2 platform revenue declined approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million due to timing of project financings and lower development fees, while total expenses rose by roughly 11% to $5.9 million driven by bad debt charges. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly from a loss in the prior period but remained below guidance targets as management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $18-$22 million without raising it.

DLocal reported Q2 FY26 TPV of $17.7 billion (up 92% YoY) and gross profit of $127 million (up 29% YoY), driven by record performance in Brazil ($40M GP) and Argentina ($20M GP). Management raised full-year guidance for TPV growth to 60%-70% and gross profit growth to 25%-30%, while maintaining operating profit growth at 27.5%-32.5%. The company highlighted strong net revenue retention of 153% and a sequential improvement in operating leverage, though it noted some FX headwinds and one-off tax impacts affecting the full-year outlook.

Revenue grew 35% year-over-year to $66.4 million driven by a net demand increase and raw material pricing impacts on tungsten and molybdenum. Adjusted EBITDA rose 57% to $8.9 million, though GAAP reported a loss of $0.16 per share due to significant one-time equity-based compensation costs associated with the IPO vesting ($12.9M). Management noted that while backlog grew significantly in defense and aerospace segments, margins were pressured by operational challenges at EMP factories dealing with high-margin AD&G products.

Enhanced Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $17.7 million driven by inaugural Enhanced Games sponsorships and early Live Enhanced activity against a backdrop of no prior-year comparable. The company posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $42.7 million, with total net loss at $61.9 million due to one-time event build costs ($52M) and transaction expenses ($10.9M). Management raised the near-term outlook for consumer growth but maintained that current results reflect a heavy investment phase rather than sustainable run rates.

EquipmentShare reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion (up 26% YoY) and rental segment revenue of $908 million (up >39% YoY). Adjusted core EBITDA grew to $531 million, representing a beat on the prior period's implied growth trajectory despite management noting that full-year guidance remains conservative for the back half. Management raised specific OWN program contribution guidance by approximately $11M and highlighted strong demand visibility in mega projects.

Euroseas reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $56.5 million and EPS of $4.74 per diluted share, representing a slight miss against the prior year's revenue growth despite higher charter rates driven by supply tightness. Management noted that while current market conditions are strong with high utilization, they anticipate potential moderation in demand towards the end of 2026 as geopolitical disruptions may ease and new vessel deliveries increase.

Eton Pharmaceuticals reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $37.6 million (up 99% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $16.2 million (43% margin). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to exceed $145 million from the prior expectation of over $120 million, citing strong performance across its pediatric dermatology franchise following HEMANGEOL's relaunch and momentum in endocrinology products.

Vertical Aerospace reported a cash burn of $112 million for the first half of FY26 and projects approximately $150 million in net outflows over the next 12 months to fund Critical Design Review (CDR) by Q4 2026. The company raised or accessed roughly $185 million since March via equity, convertible notes, and preferred equity facilities, bringing total available cash on hand to approximately $134-$148 million depending on drawdown timing. Management confirmed the aircraft is not yet certified for commercial service (targeting 2029) but highlighted progress in flight testing, ecosystem partnerships like Near Earth Autonomy, and UK government support totaling over $100 million.

FFAI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $836k (up over 1,500% YoY) and narrowed its net loss to $36M from a prior year's $124.7M due to significant cost reductions ($11.54M COGS vs $26.91M in Q2 FY25). The company raised its annual shipment target for EAI robotics units to 2,000 based on cumulative shipments of 394 through July and plans to reduce total liabilities below $100 million within the next three to four quarters.

FGI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $31.9 million (up 2.9% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 33.4%, driven by trade-related recoveries that improved GAAP operating gain to $1.4M from a prior year loss. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for adjusted net income ranging from a loss of $0.3 million to a gain of $1.1 million, explicitly stating they are looking toward the lower end of this range due to soft market conditions and cautionary inventory sentiment.

Figure reported Q2 FY26 consumer loan marketplace volume of $4.3 billion (up 132% YoY), beating the top end of guidance by 4%. Adjusted net revenue reached $218 million with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 55%, driven largely by Figure Connect now representing 65% of total volume and ecosystem fees becoming the largest P&L line item. Management raised Q3 volume guidance expectations, citing strong July performance ($1.7B) and a confident outlook for August/September.

Abeona Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $11.4 million, a 31% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by five patient treatments, though one low-yield batch and one out-of-specification batch resulted in no revenue recognition for those specific cases despite patients receiving treatment. R&D expenses decreased to $5 million from Q1's $9.6 million due to the exclusion of a one-time licensing cost incurred earlier in the year. Management highlighted operational bottlenecks including scheduling disruptions, patient health deterioration leading to cancellations, and manufacturing yield variability as key headwinds.

Newsmax reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $54.1 million (up 16.5% YoY) and achieved its first quarterly net income as a public company at $2.9 million ($0.02/share). Gross margin expanded significantly to 43.1%, driven by high-margin affiliate fees which grew 81.9% and international licensing revenue surging from $0.7M to $4.6M in the quarter. Management reiterated full-year FY26 guidance of $212-$216 million, citing structural growth led by these expanding streams.

In the first half of FY2026, YXT reported total revenues of CNY 162.1 million, a 6% year-over-year increase driven by AI product adoption and large enterprise focus. Gross margin expanded significantly to 70.1%, up five percentage points from the prior period, while net loss narrowed substantially to CNY 14.4 million. Management expressed confidence in further gross margin expansion for H2 due to continued operational efficiencies.

Valneva reported a significant miss in the first half of FY2026 with total revenues of EUR 65.8 million versus EUR 97.6 million last year and product sales declining to EUR 64 million from EUR 91 million, driven by distributor transitions for IXIARO/DUKORAL and contract phasing for the U.S. Department of Defense. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance despite these headwinds but noted that operating loss widened to EUR 49.9 million due to one-off restructuring costs (EUR 3.2M) and non-recurring inventory/write-down impacts totaling over EUR 10 million in the first half.

Suzano reported Q2 FY26 results with solid free cash flow and the successful closing of the Arbex acquisition on July 1st, though paperboard volumes were impacted by customer inventory build-up ahead of price increases. Pulp sales reached 2.9 million tons driven by higher export prices to $601/ton despite constrained production from maintenance downtimes in Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas. Management reiterated a focus on deleveraging the business following Arbex consolidation, with cash costs expected to decline below BRL 800/ton in H2 due to reduced downtime and wood consumption.

Swarmer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $216,000 compared to $138,000 in the prior year period, driven by a commercial deal where only ~$200k was recognized due to accounting treatment. Gross profit rose to roughly $184,000 from $82,000 primarily reflecting this revenue recognition mechanics rather than margin expansion on scale. Operating expenses surged to approximately $7.5 million (up from $855,000) driven by public company costs and one-time equipment purchases, resulting in a net loss of ~$7.2 million versus a prior year loss of ~$1.6 million.

Tiendas 3B reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of MXN 26 billion (up 39% YoY) and same-store sales growth of 20%. Adjusted EBITDA reached MXN 1.6 billion, reflecting a 44% increase driven by volume expansion and operational efficiencies despite one-time cash expenses related to an equity offering.

Turkcell reported Q2 FY2026 group revenue of TRY 71.8 billion (up 2.5% YoY) and net income of TRY 5.2 billion, driven by real growth despite inflation exceeding 30%. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged after revising year-end inflation expectations to around 28%, citing disciplined pricing and strong momentum in Digital Business Services (+33%) and FWA (+64k subscribers). The company crossed the 40 million mobile subscriber milestone with a postpaid base of 32.5 million, while EBITDA margin remained steady at 41.8%.

TMC reported a net loss of $60.1 million in Q2 FY2026 compared to $74.3 million in the prior year period, driven by exploration and evaluation expenses increasing significantly due to charges owed to Allseas ($37.5M) related to their development agreement signed in May. While management highlighted steady progress on U.S. permitting milestones for USA-A and USA-B applications and confirmed that cash reserves are sufficient for at least 12 months, they explicitly stated no investment decision has been made regarding the Brownsville processing site yet.

Tenon Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.3 million (up 127% YoY) and gross profit of $0.8 million with a margin expansion to 64%. The company achieved record quarterly figures driven by increased case volumes on both Catamaran and SImmetry+ platforms, while operating expenses rose due to sales/marketing spend and R&D investments in upcoming product launches.

Telesat reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of CAD 79 million and a net loss of CAD 559 million, driven by lower GEO segment revenue (down 26% YoY) due to contract expirations and satellite retirements. Management reiterated its guidance for the legacy GEO business but raised full-year investment guidance for Lightspeed from CAD 1-1.2 billion to CAD 1.3-1.5 billion following a decision to accelerate constellation expansion to 225 satellites funded by new government contracts.

Total revenue declined 20% year-over-year to $35.1 million due to a sharp drop in procurement services ($18.2M vs $33M prior year), though higher-margin systems integration grew 46%. Gross profit increased 11% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 12%, driven by the shift toward high-margin segments, but net income fell slightly to $0.05 per share due to a one-time tax valuation allowance release in Q4 FY2025 affecting comparability.

Ultrapar reported record net income of BRL 1,677 million (up 46% YoY) and recurring adjusted EBITDA of BRL 3,657 million for Q2 FY2026. The company achieved a significant working capital release at Ipiranga driven by diesel imports amid Middle East volatility, resulting in record operating cash flow generation of BRL 4.8 billion. Management anticipates margins will normalize to first-quarter levels due to the offsetting effects of fighting illegal practices and ongoing supply disruptions.

Veritone reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.3 million (up 20% sequentially and 5% YoY), but missed expectations due to delayed public sector budget shifts related to the conflict in Iran and timing issues with hyperscaler VDR deals. Management lowered fiscal 2026 full-year guidance to a range of $100-$150 million, citing reduced visibility on government contracts and specific VDR deal closures. The company executed significant cost reductions totaling approximately $11.3 million annually as of June 30, positioning for potential breakeven in the first half of fiscal 2027.

Management stated that retail disruptions in Germany and France are largely resolved but warned it will take time to return market share to neutral levels despite strong category growth of roughly 3% year-to-date. The company suspended share buybacks to focus on deleveraging while maintaining dividends, with a EUR 200 million productivity program remaining on track.

Westwater Resources reported a Q2 FY2026 consolidated net loss of $4.3 million ($0.03/share), an increase from the prior year's loss of $3.9 million due to higher permitting costs, stock-based compensation, and product development expenses. The company received a significant non-dilutive milestone in the form of a formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan dedicated exclusively to advancing Phase I construction at the Kellyton Graphite Plant. Management maintains a target timeline for commercial production starting as soon as next year (late 2026/early 2027), contingent on securing remaining capital and closing documentation.

Wolverine World Wide reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $506 million (up 7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.40 (up 14%), both exceeding expectations with the latter beating the upper end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.98B-$2.0B from $1.965B-$1.985B and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.55-$1.65 from $1.43-$1.58, citing strong H1 execution by Merrell (up 10%) and Saucony (up 9%). The company also raised its full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 46.9%.

WidePoint reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $38 million (up from $37.3M YoY) and a net loss narrowing to $66k ($0.01 EPS) compared to a prior year loss of $618k, driven by growth in carrier services but offset by lower billable fees due to partial DHS shutdowns. Management highlighted the awarding of CWMS 3.0 and SEWP VI contracts as major wins for future scale while noting that Q2 results were impacted by non-recurring items and a temporary government shutdown.

X-Energy reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $54.6 million (up 154% YoY) and operating expenses of $164.6 million due to higher ARDP work and a one-time equity comp charge, resulting in an implied loss per share as the company is newly public post-IPO. Management highlighted significant progress on supply chain de-risking with binding HALEU agreements and graphite capacity expansions, alongside a major DOE funding increase for their demonstration program. Forward guidance remains qualitative regarding project timelines (Dow permit expected late 2026) rather than quantitative financial targets.

Xunlei reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $102.7 million, up 38.9% year-over-year, driven by a 22.6% increase in subscription services and a 54.8% surge in overseas audio live streaming. However, the company posted an operating loss of $4.8 million due to higher costs associated with revenue mix shifts (lower-margin live streaming) and legal provisions, resulting in a net other loss of $230.8 million primarily from fair value volatility on investments. Management announced a new $20 million share repurchase program initiated July 1st but provided no specific guidance for the full year.

Xos reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.7 million on 30 units delivered, a decline from the prior year quarter due to order deferrals and customer acceptance delays. GAAP gross margin was 12.1% for the quarter but improved significantly in H1 with a record 31%, while operating loss narrowed sequentially despite lower volumes. Management revised full-year guidance downward, projecting revenue between $35 million and $43 million.

YETI reported Q2 FY26 sales of $484 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.67 (up 2%), with gross margin expanding 170 bps to 59.5%. Management raised full-year operating margin guidance by 30 bps to approximately 14.9%, citing strong operational execution, pricing discipline, and the benefit from IEPA tariff refunds partially offsetting inflationary pressures.

York Space Systems reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $92.5 million (up 10% YoY) and a gross margin expansion to 24%, but adjusted EBITDA remained at an $8.9M-$9.5M loss due to increased SG&A from acquisitions. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance down significantly, lowering the midpoint by $180 million to $375M-$405M as IDIQ contract awards shifted recognition into 2027 and supply chain delays pushed out delivery.

Yesway reported a record second quarter with adjusted EBITDA of $71 million (up 35% YoY) and store contribution rising to $88 million. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range from $210-$220 million to $235-$245 million, driven by strong fuel volume growth of 1.4% same-store (excluding sold stores) and inside merchandise sales up 4.4%. The company ended the quarter with a store count of 450 after opening one new location.

StoneCo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of BRL 3.6 billion and adjusted gross profit that was broadly stable year-over-year at BRL 1.6 billion due to higher revenues offset by provision expenses from credit portfolio growth. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted gross profits (BRL 6.6-7bn) but noted the backdrop is more challenging than anticipated, with a focus on delivering toward the lower end of ranges given elevated interest rates and macro headwinds. TPV growth accelerated to 4% annually as retention initiatives began showing traction.

Stantec reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of CAD 1.8 billion (up ~12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to a record 18.7%. Management raised the full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 17.8%-18.3%, citing strong backlog growth, particularly in water and global regions, while noting Q2 U.S. organic growth was impacted by timing issues rather than demand weakness.

Stratasys reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $137.6 million, which was flat year-over-year despite a sequential increase driven by record consumable sales ($66.3M). Management reaffirmed full-year guidance but lowered the operating cash flow outlook for the year due to non-routine legal expenses in Q2 and expects positive cash flow only from H2 2026.

Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining reported a net loss of $16.7 million ($0.13 per share) for Q2 FY2026, an increase from the prior year's loss due to accelerated development activities and IPO-related costs. The company raised approximately $310 million in its recent IPO, bringing cash on hand to $288.7 million at quarter-end with no long-term debt. Management provided a clear path toward production targeted for late 2028 but declined to provide specific financial guidance or updated spending forecasts beyond noting that G&A will taper off starting Q1 2027.

Nu Holdings reported a historic quarter with net income exceeding $1 billion for the first time ($1.1B), driven by gross revenue of nearly $5.9 billion and record risk-adjusted NIM expanding to 12.4%. The company achieved this while maintaining an efficiency ratio near its long-term target of 20% despite sequential operating expense increases due to international expansion investments.

Nuwellis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.97 million (up 14% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 76%, driven by pricing adjustments and product mix shifts rather than volume growth, which remained low with only nine consoles sold in the quarter compared to three last year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $4.8 million, including roughly $1.7 million in warrant valuation expense from recent financing activities that strengthened cash reserves but did not provide formal financial guidance for future periods.

Ondas reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.8 million (up >13x YoY) and adjusted gross margin stable at 50.4%. Management raised the full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $525-$550 million, citing strong organic growth drivers including Sentrycs (+298% pro forma), Airobotics (+112%), and 4M (+258%). The company ended with approximately $1.4 billion in cash equivalents after deploying capital for new acquisitions.

OptimumBank reported record quarterly net income of $6.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.28 for Q2 FY2026, representing a significant increase over the prior quarter and year-ago period driven by loan growth and NIM expansion to 4.57%. Management raised its forward-looking annual earnings estimate range from approximately $1 per share to between $1 and $1.15 per share based on the current quarterly run rate of $0.28, which they believe is easily replicable going forward.

Q2 attributable silver production of 6.5 million ounces met the high end of guidance driven by La Colorada and Juanicipio, while gold production missed outlook due to seismic mitigation at Jacobina and continuity issues at El Peñón. Management reaffirmed full-year operating ranges but lowered Q3 gold expectations and noted higher tax expenses ($179M) impacting net earnings compared to consensus estimates. The company returned a record $300 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, maintaining strong liquidity of approximately $3.2 billion.

Second quarter net revenue increased 9% year-over-year to $23 million, driven by an 8% increase in firearm sales and a shift toward higher price-point products. Gross margin expanded significantly from 10.6% to approximately 13.5%, while operating expenses rose sharply due to incremental costs associated with becoming a public company and scaling PEW Logistics. The quarter ended the transition period for like-for-like expense comparisons, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.7 million compared to prior year income.

PLDT reported first-half FY26 service revenues of PHP 108.7 billion (up 2% YoY) and EBITDA of PHP 56.1 billion at a stable 52% margin, though Telco core income declined 2% to PHP 16.6 billion due to higher depreciation. Wireless revenue was broadly flat while Home revenues fell 1% following Q1 installation constraints that are now recovering in the second quarter with positive net adds starting in May. Enterprise remained a strong growth driver up 5%, and management reiterated full-year CapEx guidance of mid-PHP 50 billion despite elevated depreciation from network upgrades.

Pelagos Insurance Capital reported Q2 FY26 gross premiums written of $1.3 billion (up 6% YoY) and operating net income of $29 million ($0.34 diluted EPS). The quarter's combined ratio was elevated at 99.5%, driven by large loss events totaling $162 million, including specific losses from the Middle East conflict and a gas plant explosion in Qatar; however, management views this as random timing variability rather than an underlying trend deterioration. Management maintained its full-year guidance for mid-single-digit growth and ROAE targets of 13%-15%, citing that H1 results are broadly on plan with Q3/Q4 expected to normalize the combined ratio.

ProMIS Neurosciences reported a net loss of CAD 11.7 million (CAD $1.28 per share) for Q2 FY26, compared to a prior year loss of CAD 10.1 million, driven by increased R&D and G&A expenses as the company advanced its clinical programs. The quarter was defined by positive blinded interim data from the Phase I-B PRECISE-AD trial showing zero ARIA-E cases across all genotypes (including ApoE4 homozygotes) and early biomarker declines consistent with target engagement, though no financial guidance or revenue beat exists as this is a clinical-stage company. Management indicated cash on hand of CAD 53.4 million provides runway through late 2027 to fund operations until the anticipated Q1 FY27 top-line readout.

Pershing Square Inc reported its first quarter earnings for FY26 but provided no specific revenue or EPS figures in the transcript, focusing instead on strategic updates regarding its IPO vehicle PSUS and future fund launches. Management acknowledged that PSUS is trading at a significant discount to NAV (approximate $50 vs high 30s) due to low volume and retail over-subscription issues they intend to fix with increased marketing efforts. The company confirmed plans for Pershing Square Ventures in late Q4 FY26 and discussed the SPARC vehicle as an efficient way to take private companies public, though no specific deal has been closed yet.

Pelthos Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 net product revenue of $15.4 million, a 45% increase from the prior quarter and driven by a 48% rise in prescribed units to 11,925. Gross-to-net margins were favorable at 29.6%, slightly up from Q1 but below management's mid-30% long-term target due to ongoing payer contract negotiations. The company restated its Q1 financials regarding convertible debt fair value accounting, which impacted reported net loss and adjusted EBITDA figures for the period.

QSI reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $344,000 (down from $591,000 in the prior year) and a net loss of $23.5 million, while maintaining full-year guidance for approximately $1M revenue despite announcing significant cost-cutting measures including a 20% reduction in force. Management delayed the Proteus launch timeline to Q2 FY2027 from late 2026 following internal testing that revealed manufacturing repeatability risks requiring an additional design cycle before production.

SABESP reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net revenue growth of 9.4% year-over-year driven by tariff increases and customer expansion, while Adjusted EBITDA declined 3.2% to BRL 3.5 billion due to higher costs from inflationary pressures (chemicals), investments in commercial initiatives (~BRL 800 million annualized spend), and ERP timing effects. Management provided a cautious outlook on underlying cost normalization for the second half of the year, noting that roughly 75-80% of current elevated OpEx is expected to be recovered through future tariff cycles or productivity gains by 2027.

Stardust Power reported a net loss of $3.9 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $3.7 million in the prior year period and remains pre-revenue as it advances development activities at its Muskogee refinery site. The company clarified that no forward-looking guidance or estimates would be provided during this call, focusing instead on past performance and current financial position including cash of approximately $0.5 million. Management highlighted recent capital raises via an ELOC and ATM facility to support working capital needs while maintaining disciplined liquidity management.

Securitize reported Q2 FY2026 results as a newly public company but did not disclose specific revenue or EPS figures in the provided transcript text. Management highlighted that AUM recovered to $4.2 billion and exceeded $5 billion by early Q3, while asset servicing revenue remains stable with modest quarterly growth expected for the remainder of 2026. The company reiterated a wide full-year guidance range due to project dependencies on third-party institutional timelines.

CSN reported a consolidated EBITDA increase of 5% year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter to BRL 6 billion for Q2 FY2026, driven by record performance in cement (EBITDA >BRL 420 million) and logistics. However, the mining segment saw net revenue decline due to a 15-day shutdown and foreign exchange impacts, while steel margins recovered but remain under pressure from raw material costs. Management highlighted significant working capital releases of approximately BRL 900-1 billion projected by year-end as key drivers for cash flow.

Second quarter revenue was $113 million compared to a prior year of $215 million, driven by unfavorable legacy dispute adjustments totaling approximately $102 million in revenue reversals and $94 million impacting gross loss. Gross loss for the quarter reached $71 million versus a profit of $13 million last year due to these non-cash catch-up adjustments on derecognized claim positions. Management finalized strategic agreements with sureties providing financing support, restructuring debt terms including interest capitalization, and expects bidding activity to increase in the back half of 2026.

Soluna reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $15.1 million (up 145% YoY) and a net loss of $22.6 million compared to $7.8 million in the prior year, driven by non-cash stock-based compensation ($9.4M), interest expense increases, and debt extinguishment losses following capital raises totaling ~$183M. Management raised guidance for operating capacity from 192 MW at quarter-end to an expected 206 MW by summer end due to the energization of Kati 1 Phase 3. The company acquired a $53M wind farm and consolidated ownership of Project Dorothy, while advancing two major AI campuses (Kati 2 and Dorothy 3) toward construction.

ARS Pharma reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $26.2 million and total operating expenses of $95.1 million with gross margins at approximately 62%. Management announced a significant strategic pivot to reduce SG&A by over 40% in the second half, projecting cash-flow breakeven by end-2027 rather than raising near-term revenue guidance.

ADI reported record quarterly revenue of $1.29 billion and segment adjusted EBITDA of $103 million on a carve-out basis for Q2 FY26, beating the high end of prior guidance provided by Resideo. However, standalone adjusted EBITDA was $86 million with margins pressured by higher operating expenses, freight costs, tariff impacts, and an exclusive brands revenue decline of nearly 3%. Management initiated full-year 2026 guidance expecting mid-single-digit second-half growth but noted continued gross margin headwinds from supplier transitions and difficult prior-year comparisons.

BrainsWay reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.1 million (up 35% YoY) and operating income increasing over 300% to $2.4 million. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance from a range of $66M-$68M to $68M-$70M, citing strong demand for the SWIFT protocol and growing remaining performance obligations of $80.4 million.

Vuzix reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.1 million, a decrease of 14% year-over-year from $1.3 million in the prior period. The company posted a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $7.7 million ($0.09 per share), compared to $7.7 million and $0.10 per share respectively in Q2 FY2025, with gross losses narrowing by 15% despite higher R&D expenses driven by new product development costs.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $27.2 million (up 16% YoY), but gross margins contracted to 65.7%, operating loss widened to $5.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA missed at -$2.3M versus prior year profit of +$1.1M due to ExoDx integration costs. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $110-115M but warned that Q4/Q1 will face headwinds from tissue-based business restructuring and the wind-down of discontinued Resolve operations.

Paysafe reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $447.4 million (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $102.8 million (down 2%), resulting in an EPS miss due to increased marketing/IT investments and interest expenses despite the resolution of legacy litigation matters. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue and adjusted EBITDA while updating adjusted EPS expectations, citing a strong first-half growth rate of 7% that met prior outlooks.

NACG reported Q2 2026 combined revenue of CAD 456M, up from CAD 370M a year ago, with EBITDA of CAD 93M and adjusted EPS of CAD 0.32. Australia grew organically 15% excluding IMC, and the company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint by CAD 100M to CAD 1.7B. Management reiterated adjusted EBITDA guidance of CAD 380-420M and free cash flow of CAD 110-130M, highlighting record backlog of CAD 3.8B and a strong bid pipeline.

Total revenue for Q2 FY26 was approximately $0.2 million compared to negative $21k in the prior year period due to a one-time accounting adjustment and delayed product launch timing (Flora Sync LF5 sales began July). Net loss improved from $4M to $3M, driven by lower R&D expenses offset by non-cash write-downs of deferred offering costs. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated revenue recognition for DARE to PLAY will begin in Q3 and DARE to RECLAIM is targeted for 2027.

SoundThinking reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $23.9 million (down from $25.9M prior year) and GAAP net loss widening to $4.8 million ($0.37/share), though Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.2 million due to cost reductions. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance down significantly to a range of $99-$100 million (from prior expectations near $110M) citing delays in SafePointe deployments, Puerto Rico contract issues, and ShotSpotter sales cycle elongation driven by political scrutiny and funding constraints. The company maintains confidence in its long-term recurring revenue base but acknowledges the need to underwrite a longer sales cycle.

LENSAR reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.5 million (up 18% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million, its strongest quarterly performance to date driven by recurring revenue growth to $13.7 million and a one-time tariff refund benefit. The company raised guidance implicitly through strong execution despite noting that operating expenses will normalize higher in future quarters as commercial investments resume following the terminated merger with Alcon.

Q2 FY26 revenue was $5.9 million (up 16% YoY), with gross margin at 91%, adjusted EBITDA of $1.1M, and net income of $633k. Management noted that a major customer's vendor review is not yet causing the volume reductions previously feared, though full-year revenue for FY2026 may be slightly lower than FY2025 if plans proceed as communicated. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $11.8M in cash and no debt.

Grandstand reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $37.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of $7.7 million, both in line with expectations but representing a 5% year-over-year decline due to lower marketing revenue offsetting strong data growth ($11.2M). The company reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $165-$170 million and adjusted EBITDA between $45-$50 million, noting that the current run rate implies modest flat-to-low-single-digit annual growth rather than a significant beat or raise.

Q2 FY2026 revenue grew sequentially by approximately 79% to $1.7 million and annually by 42%, driven primarily by the EngineRoom acquisition which contributed one month of combined revenue in June ($8M total run-rate). Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) jumped from $3.6M to $11.5M, while Net Revenue Retention improved to 99.3%. Management provided no specific financial guidance for Q3 or beyond but indicated a directional path toward breakeven by the second half of FY2027.

AudioEye reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $10.7 million (up 9% YoY) and ARR growth to $42.3 million. The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance from at least $12 million to at least $12.7 million, driven by record Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $3 million ($0.23/share). Management expects litigation expenses to trend down in the second half and is evaluating options for excess cash deployment including buybacks or dividends.

Enovix reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $9 million (up 21% YoY), which landed at the high end of guidance but missed analyst consensus expectations due to a lack of specific beat confirmation in the text. The company recorded its first smart eyewear product revenue and advanced smartphone qualification milestones, though gross margins were pressured by South Korea mix shifts resulting in GAAP margins of 14.4%. Management maintained Q3 revenue guidance between $9-10 million but did not raise it despite strong pipeline growth.

ERock reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $39.9 million (up 26% sequentially) and a net loss of $67.7 million driven by non-recurring IPO-related debt extinguishment losses totaling $48.8 million, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA miss relative to the prior quarter's -$12.4M as guidance was not yet issued at that time but implied positive H2 2026. Management provided full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $435-$465 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3-$9 million, projecting a return to profitability in the second half driven by backlog conversion.

Net revenue grew 2.5% to $499 million while adjusted comparable store sales increased 2.2%, driven by a 7.1% average ticket expansion that offset a 4.9% decline in traffic. Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3% and adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 per share, though management narrowed the full-year top-line guidance range due to persistent deferrals from lower-value transactions following an e-commerce re-platform.

Journey Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $18.5 million, a 23% year-over-year increase driven by Emrosi net product revenues of $8.1 million and improved ASPs. The company achieved positive GAAP EBITDA ($1.4M) and adjusted EBITDA ($2.9M), narrowing its loss to $0.01 per share compared to a prior period loss of $3.8M. Management highlighted accelerating prescription growth for Emrosi (up 20% sequentially) but noted that SG&A expenses remained elevated due to launch-related spending and upcoming marketing programs, with no specific guidance raised.

Phoenix New Media reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of RMB 216.7 million, a 15.8% year-over-year increase driven by paid services growth (RMB 69.8 million) and net advertising revenues of RMB 146.9 million. Gross margin expanded significantly to 57.3%, while operating expenses rose 30.4% due to digital reading initiatives, resulting in a narrow loss from operations but an improved net income attributable to the company compared to the prior year's loss. Management provided Q3 guidance of RMB 220.9 million to RMB 235.9 million total revenue and noted that while advertising demand was mixed due to contract timing issues, they see a structural shift toward content-driven monetization.

Franco-Nevada reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $348 million (implied by context) with adjusted net income and EPS up 46% year-over-year driven by record gold prices (+38%) and higher production at Antamina, South Arturo, Côté Gold, Casa Berardi, and Valentine. The company sold 132,405 total GEOs (up 18%), tracking toward the upper half of its full-year guidance range of 510,000-570,000 units despite a slight pullback in precious metal prices from Q1 highs.

Fossil Group reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $211 million (a 4% decline YoY) and gross margins expanding to 62.4%. Management raised full-year guidance for worldwide net sales to a 3%-5% decline range from the prior 4%-6%, while also raising adjusted operating margin expectations to 4%-6%.

Forward Industries reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $10.8 million (up from $2.5M prior year) and a gross margin expansion to 62.2%, though the quarter included significant unrealized losses on digital assets totaling $49.8 million resulting in a net loss of $69.0 million ($0.8/share). Management highlighted strong operational execution with SOL per share growing 36% annualized, index inclusion into Russell indices, and successful deployment of capital via ATM issuances and buybacks to accrete value.

Commercial sales for the quarter were $0.4 million compared to $0.1 million in Q2 FY2025, while six-month commercial sales reached $0.9 million versus $0.2 million last year due to a rebuilding of the commercial team and inventory write-downs totaling $2.3 million over the half-year. The company reported a net loss of $36.8 million for Q2 FY2026, driven by non-cash remeasurement of contingent earnout liabilities rather than operational cash burn which remained positive at $29.4 million in H1. Management provided no updated financial guidance but reaffirmed the plan to file a supplemental BLA for dialysis access in November 2026 with an anticipated launch target in Q2 FY2027.

Fervo Energy reported a Q2 FY2026 operating loss of $28.7 million and net loss of $55.9 million as it ramps up construction at Cape Station with capital expenditures reaching $226.5 million in the quarter. Management provided non-GAAP revenue guidance for 2027 between $60 million and $80 million, explicitly noting this range is wider than usual due to potential curtailment events during initial commercial operations that are outside their control. While pipeline progress remains strong with significant capacity moved into advanced development and a record-breaking drilling pace demonstrated by the Sawtooth 7 well, immediate financial performance reflects pre-revenue burn.

Global-E reported Q2 FY26 results with GMV of $2.1 billion (up 44% YoY) and revenue of $299 million (up 39% YoY), significantly beating the high end of prior guidance. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for GMV, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA to reflect strong momentum from new brand launches, Managed Markets V2 adoption, and the recently closed acquisition of Passport. Adjusted EBITDA reached $62.4 million (a margin of ~21%), representing a more than 300 bps expansion compared to Q2 FY25.

Revenue increased 1% to $1.19 billion while comparable store sales declined 30 basis points due to Easter timing and a Cyclospora outbreak headwind expected in Q3. Adjusted EPS of $0.20 beat the outlook, driven by gross margin expansion to 30.2% from lower promotional spending despite flat gross profit dollars. Management raised full-year net sales guidance slightly but maintained comparable store sales expectations near zero.

Harmonic reported Q2 FY26 broadband revenue of $133.5 million (up 54% YoY), significantly beating the high end of guidance ($115M-$125M) and EPS of $0.21, which beat the range of $0.15-$0.19. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a new range of $505 million to $525 million (up from prior $475M-$495M), citing record backlog and strong rest-of-market growth. The company completed its transformation into a pure-play broadband entity following the sale of its video business.
